title.zh: 卷三百九十五 列傳第一百五十四 樓鑰 李大性 任希夷 徐應龍 莊夏 王阮 王質 陸游 方信孺 王柟
title.en: Volume 395 Biographies 154: Lou Yao, Li Daxing, Ren Xiyi, Xu Yinglong, Zhuang Xia, Wang Ruan, Wang Zhi, Lu You, Fang Xinru, Wang Nan
title.raw: 卷三百九十五 列傳第一百五十四 樓鑰 李大性 任希夷 徐應龍 莊夏 王阮 王質 陸游 方信孺 王柟 Volume 395 Biographies 154: Lou Yao, Li Daxing, Ren Xiyi, Xu Yinglong, Zhuang Xia, Wang Ruan, Wang Zhi, Lu You, Fang Xinru, Wang Nan

sentences.zh: 樓鑰，字大防，明州鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Lou Yao, styled Dafang, was a native of Yin County in Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Yao, courtesy name Dafang, came from Yin County in Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，試南宮，有司偉其辭藝，欲以冠多士，策偶犯舊諱，知貢舉洪遵奏，得旨以冠末等。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, he tested at the Southern Palace examination; the officials admired his literary skill and wished to place him first among the successful candidates, but his policy essay accidentally violated an old taboo name; Hong Zun, the chief examiner, memorialized, and he received the imperial decision to be ranked last among the top tier.
translations.idiomatic: In Longxing 1 (1163), he sat for the metropolitan examination. The examiners admired his writing and intended to rank him first, but his policy essay inadvertently violated an old naming taboo. Chief examiner Hong Zun reported this, and by imperial order Lou was placed last among the highest tier of graduates.

sentences.zh: 投贄謝諸公，考官胡銓稱之曰：「此翰林才也。」

translations.literal: Presenting a letter of thanks to the examiners, the examiner Hu Quan praised him, saying: "This is talent fit for the Hanlin Academy."
translations.idiomatic: When he submitted a letter of thanks to the examiners, Hu Quan, one of the examiners, praised him: "This man has the makings of a Hanlin academician."

sentences.zh: 試教官，調溫州教授，為敕令所刪定官，修《淳熙法》。

translations.literal: He passed the instructor examination, was assigned as professor at Wenzhou, served as a reviser at the Edicts and Ordinances Office, and compiled the Chunxi Code.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the instructor examination, was appointed professor at Wenzhou, served as a reviser at the Edicts and Ordinances Office, and helped compile the Chunxi Code.

sentences.zh: 議者欲降太學釋奠為中祀，鑰曰：「乘輿臨幸，於先聖則拜，武成則肅揖，其禮異矣，可鈞敵乎？」

translations.literal: Some in debate wished to downgrade the Imperial Academy's sacrifice to Confucius to a medium-grade rite; Yao said: "When the imperial carriage visits in person, one bows to the Former Sage but performs a solemn bow with hands clasped to Wu Cheng — the rites already differ; can they be made equal?"
translations.idiomatic: Debaters proposed lowering the Imperial Academy's Confucian sacrifice from a major to a medium-grade rite. Lou objected: "When the emperor visits in person, he bows to Confucius but only performs a formal clasped-hand salute at the Wu Cheng shrine — the ceremonies are already unequal. How can they be treated as equivalent?"

sentences.zh: 改宗正寺主簿，歷太府、宗正寺丞，出知溫州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Clan, successively served as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Granary and of the Court of the Imperial Clan, and was sent out as prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Clan, then served successively as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Granary and of the Court of the Imperial Clan before being appointed prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬縣樂清倡言方臘之變且復起，邑令捕數人歸於郡。

translations.literal: In a subordinate county, Yueqing, people spread word that Fang La's rebellion was about to rise again; the county magistrate arrested several men and sent them to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Yueqing, a county under his jurisdiction, rumors spread that another uprising like Fang La's was imminent. The county magistrate arrested several men and sent them to the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 鑰曰：「罪之則無可坐，縱之則惑民。」

translations.literal: Yao said: "If we punish them, there is no crime on which to convict them; if we release them, the people will be unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: Lou said: "If we punish them, there is no charge that will stand; if we release them, we will only alarm the people."

sentences.zh: 編隸其為首者，而驅其徒出境，民言遂定。

translations.literal: He registered the ringleaders for corvée labor and drove their followers out of the region, and the people's talk then subsided.
translations.idiomatic: He enrolled the ringleaders in corvée registers and expelled their followers from the region, and public alarm soon died down.

sentences.zh: 堂帖問故，鑰曰：「蘇洵有言：『有亂之形，無亂之實，是謂將亂。

translations.literal: A palace directive asked the reason; Yao said: "Su Xun once said: 'There is the form of disorder without the reality of disorder — that is what is called impending disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When a palace directive asked for an explanation, Lou cited Su Xun: "There is the shape of rebellion without the substance of rebellion — that is what is called rebellion about to break out.

sentences.zh: 不可以有亂急，不可以無亂弛。』」

translations.literal: One must not treat it as rebellion and grow tense; one must not treat it as no rebellion and grow lax.'
translations.idiomatic: One must not respond as though rebellion were already here and grow frantic; one must not treat it as nothing and grow complacent."

sentences.zh: 丞相周必大心善之。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Zhou Bida was greatly pleased at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Zhou Bida was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 光宗嗣位，召對，奏曰：「人主初政，當先立其大者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong succeeded to the throne, Yao was summoned for an audience and memorialized: "At the outset of a ruler's reign, he should first establish what is greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong ascended the throne, Lou was summoned to court and said: "At the beginning of a reign, a ruler should first set his priorities on what matters most.

sentences.zh: 至大莫如恢復，然當先強主志，進君德。」

translations.literal: Nothing is greater than recovery of lost territory, yet one should first strengthen the ruler's resolve and advance his virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is greater than recovering the north, but the emperor must first strengthen his own resolve and cultivate his moral authority."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「今之網密甚矣，望陛下軫念元元，以設禁為不得已，凡有創意增益者，寢而勿行，所以保養元氣。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The net of prohibitions is now very tight; I hope Your Majesty will pity the common people, treat the imposition of bans as a last resort, and let lie fallow any new proposals that add restrictions — thus preserving the nation's vital energy."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Regulations have grown exceedingly tight. I hope Your Majesty will have compassion for the people, treat new prohibitions as measures of last resort, and set aside any fresh restrictions — thus preserving the nation's vital strength."

sentences.zh: 除考功郎兼禮部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of Personnel in the Ministry of Personnel, with concurrent duty in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 吏銓並緣為姦，多所壅底。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel had long been entangled in fraud, and many matters were blocked and delayed.
translations.idiomatic: The personnel ministry had become riddled with corruption, and business piled up unresolved.

sentences.zh: 鑰曰：「簡要清通，尚書郎之選。」

translations.literal: Yao said: "Simplicity, clarity, and efficiency — these are what a director of a ministry should possess."
translations.idiomatic: Lou said: "Brevity, clarity, and efficiency — that is what a ministry director should embody."

sentences.zh: 盡革去之。

translations.literal: He abolished all such abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He swept the abuses away.

sentences.zh: 改國子司業，擢起居郎兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, then promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat and concurrently Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, then was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat and concurrently Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 代言坦明，得制誥體，繳奏無所回避。

translations.literal: His drafted edicts were plain and clear, in the proper style of imperial pronouncements; in submitting rebuttals he never evaded difficult issues.
translations.idiomatic: His drafted edicts were straightforward and lucid, in proper memorial style, and when submitting rebuttals he never shied from controversy.

sentences.zh: 禁中或私請，上曰：「樓舍人朕亦憚之，不如且已。」

translations.literal: Within the palace someone privately made a request; the emperor said: "Drafting Secretary Lou — even I am wary of him; better leave it for now."
translations.idiomatic: When someone in the inner palace privately solicited a favor, the emperor said: "Even I am afraid of Drafting Secretary Lou — we'd better drop this."

sentences.zh: 刑部言，天下獄案多所奏裁，中書之務不清，宜痛省之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice reported that prison cases throughout the empire were frequently submitted for imperial decision, leaving the secretariat's business unclear; it should be sharply reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice argued that criminal cases across the empire were too often referred to the throne for final judgment, leaving the secretariat's work in disarray, and urged drastic reduction.

sentences.zh: 鑰曰：「三宥制刑，古有明訓。」

translations.literal: Yao said: "The three grounds for pardon in imposing punishment — this is an ancient and explicit teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Lou replied: "The ancient doctrine of the three grounds for mercy in sentencing is explicit."

sentences.zh: 力論不可。

translations.literal: He forcefully argued that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: He argued forcefully against the proposal.

sentences.zh: 會慶節上壽，扈從班集，乘輿不出。

translations.literal: When the celebration of the emperor's birthday arrived, the entourage assembled in attendance, but the imperial carriage did not appear.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's birthday, the entourage assembled as usual, but the emperor did not appear.

sentences.zh: 已而玉牒、聖政、會要書成，將進重華，又屢更日。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the imperial genealogy, records of sagely governance, and institutional compendium were completed and were to be presented at Chonghua Palace, yet the date was repeatedly postponed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the imperial genealogy, Sagely Governance records, and institutional compendium were ready to be presented at Chonghua Palace, but the date was put off again and again.

sentences.zh: 鑰言：「臣累歲隨班，見陛下上壽重華宮，歡動宸極。

translations.literal: Yao said: "For years I have followed the entourage and seen Your Majesty attend birthday celebrations at Chonghua Palace, moving the whole court with joy.
translations.idiomatic: Lou said: "For years I have stood in attendance and watched Your Majesty celebrate the retired emperor's birthday at Chonghua Palace with evident joy.

sentences.zh: 嘉王日趨朝謁，恪勤不懈，竊料壽皇望陛下之來，亦猶此也。」

translations.literal: Prince Jia attends court daily with tireless diligence; I venture to suppose that Emperor Shouhuang awaits Your Majesty's visit with the same longing."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jia attends court every day with unwavering diligence. I can only imagine that the retired emperor waits for Your Majesty with the same expectation."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「聖政之書，全載壽皇一朝之事。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The book of sagely governance fully records the reign of Emperor Shouhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The Sagely Governance compendium preserves the entire record of Shouhuang's reign.

sentences.zh: 玉牒、會要足成淳熙末年之書，幸速定其日，無復再展，以全聖孝。」

translations.literal: The imperial genealogy and institutional compendium complete the books of the late Chunxi era; I pray that the date be fixed quickly and not postponed again, so as to fulfill filial duty fully."
translations.idiomatic: The genealogy and institutional records complete the documentation of the late Chunxi period. Please fix a date at once and do not delay again, so that filial duty may be fully observed."

sentences.zh: 於是上感悟，進書成禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor was moved to understanding, and the presentation ceremony was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved, and the presentation ceremony went forward.

sentences.zh: 試中書舍人，俄兼直學士院。

translations.literal: He passed the drafting secretary examination and soon concurrently served in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination for drafting secretary and soon held concurrent appointment in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 光宗內禪詔書，鑰所草也，有云：「雖喪紀自行於宮中，而禮文難示於天下。」

translations.literal: The edict on Guangzong's inner abdication was drafted by Yao; it contained the words: "Although mourning observances are carried out within the palace, the ritual forms are hard to display to the world."
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong's abdication edict was drafted by Lou. It read in part: "Though mourning rites may be observed within the palace, the ceremonial forms cannot easily be shown to the world."

sentences.zh: 薦紳傳誦之。

translations.literal: The gentry repeated and circulated it.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and scholars circulated the passage widely.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the post of Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 乞正太祖東向之位，別立僖祖廟以代夾室，順祖、翼祖、宣祖之主皆藏其中，祫祭即廟而饗。

translations.literal: He requested that Taizu's tablet face east be corrected, that a separate temple for Prince Xi be established in place of the side chamber, that the tablets of Shunzu, Yizu, and Xuanzu all be housed within it, and that at the great seasonal sacrifice offerings be made at the temple itself.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to restore Taizu's east-facing tablet, establish a separate temple to Prince Xi in place of the side chamber, enshrine the tablets of Shunzu, Yizu, and Xuanzu there, and perform the great seasonal offerings at that temple.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 朱熹以論事忤韓侂胄，除職與郡。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi, for remonstrating on policy, offended Han Tuozhou and was given an appointment in the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi offended Han Tuozhou by his policy remonstrances and was sent to a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 鑰言：「熹鴻儒碩學，陛下閔其耆老，當此隆寒，立講不便，何如俾之內祠，仍令修史，少俟春和，復還講筵。」

translations.literal: Yao said: "Xi is a great Confucian scholar; Your Majesty, pitying his advanced age, finds it inconvenient to have him lecture in this bitter cold — would it not be better to give him an inner-court sinecure, still charge him with compiling history, wait until spring warmth returns, and then restore him to the lecture hall?
translations.idiomatic: Lou argued: "Xi is a towering scholar. Your Majesty, out of concern for his age, finds it awkward to have him lecture in this bitter cold — why not appoint him to an inner-court post, keep him compiling history, and restore him to the lecture hall when spring comes?"

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 趙汝愚謂人曰：「樓公當今人物也，直恐臨事少剛決耳。」

translations.literal: Zhao Ruyu said to someone: "Master Lou is a leading figure of our age, but I only fear he may lack firmness in a crisis."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu remarked: "Master Lou is among the finest men of the day, but I worry he may prove insufficiently resolute when matters come to a head."

sentences.zh: 及見其持論堅正，歎曰：「吾於是大過所望矣。」

translations.literal: When he saw Yao's arguments steadfast and correct, he sighed and said: "I have now greatly exceeded my expectations of him."
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Lou hold his ground with unwavering principle, he exclaimed: "He has far surpassed what I hoped for."

sentences.zh: 寧宗受禪，侂胄以知閤門事與聞傳命，頗有弄權之漸，彭龜年力攻之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong received the abdication, Tuozhou, as Director of the Palace Gate Office, took part in transmitting the command and gradually showed signs of manipulating power; Peng Guinian forcefully attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong accepted the throne, Tuozhou — then Director of the Palace Gate Office — helped transmit the succession decree and gradually began to manipulate power. Peng Guinian attacked him forcefully.

sentences.zh: 侂胄轉一官，與在京宮觀，龜年除待制，與郡。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was transferred one rank and given a metropolitan sinecure; Guinian was made a Hanlin academician and sent to the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou received a one-rank promotion and a metropolitan sinecure; Guinian was made Hanlin academician and sent to a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 鑰與林大中奏，乞留龜年於講筵，或命侂胄以外祠。

translations.literal: Yao and Lin Dazhong memorialized, asking that Guinian be kept at the lecture hall, or that Tuozhou be given an outer-court sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Lou and Lin Dazhong memorialized to keep Guinian at the lecture hall, or to assign Tuozhou to an outer-court sinecure.

sentences.zh: 龜年竟去，鑰遷為吏部尚書，以顯謨閣學士提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: Guinian left in the end; Yao was promoted to Minister of Personnel and, as Academician of the Xianmo Pavilion, was appointed to administer the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guinian departed after all. Lou was promoted to Minister of Personnel and, as Xianmo Pavilion academician, was put in charge of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋知婺州，移寧國府，罷，仍奪職。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Wuzhou, then transferred to Ningguo Prefecture; he was dismissed and also stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Wuzhou, then transferred to Ningguo Prefecture, dismissed, and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 告老至再，許之。

translations.literal: He twice requested retirement and was permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned twice for retirement and was granted leave.

sentences.zh: 侂胄嘗副鑰為館伴，以鑰不附己，深嗛之。

translations.literal: Tuozhou had once served as Yao's deputy in receiving envoys; because Yao would not side with him, he deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou had once served as Lou's deputy when receiving foreign envoys. Because Lou would not align with him, Tuozhou deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，詔起鑰為翰林學士，遷吏部尚書兼翰林侍講。

translations.literal: After Tuozhou was executed, an edict recalled Yao as Hanlin Academician and promoted him to Minister of Personnel, concurrently Hanlin Attendant Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuozhou's execution, an edict recalled Lou as Hanlin Academician and Minister of Personnel, concurrently Hanlin Attendant Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 時鑰年過七十，精敏絕人，詞頭下，立進草，院吏驚詫。

translations.literal: By then Yao was over seventy, yet his keenness surpassed others; when a draft edict was issued, he at once submitted a draft, to the astonishment of the academy clerks.
translations.idiomatic: By then Lou was over seventy, yet still sharper than men half his age. When an edict draft was ordered, he produced one on the spot, astonishing the academy staff.

sentences.zh: 入朝，陛循舊班諦視鑰曰：「久不見此官矣。」

translations.literal: Entering court, the emperor, following the old order, looked closely at Yao and said: "It has been long since I have seen this office filled."
translations.idiomatic: At court the emperor, scanning the old roster, looked closely at Lou and said: "It has been a long time since anyone held this post properly."

sentences.zh: 時和好未定，金求韓侂胄函首，鑰曰：「和好待此而決，姦凶已斃之首，又何足恤。」

translations.literal: At the time peace had not yet been settled; Jin demanded Han Tuozhou's head in a box; Yao said: "Peace waits on this decision; what need is there to worry over the head of a traitor already dead?"
translations.idiomatic: Peace with Jin was still unsettled, and the Jurchens demanded Han Tuozhou's head in a box. Lou said: "Peace hinges on this — why fret over the head of a villain already dead?"

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 趙汝愚之子崇憲奏雪父冤，鑰乞正趙師召之罪，重蔡璉之誅，毀龔頤正《續稽古錄》以白誣謗。

translations.literal: Zhao Ruyu's son Chongxian memorialized to clear his father's wrongful conviction; Yao asked to rectify Zhao Shizhao's crime, reaffirm Cai Lian's punishment, and destroy Gong Yizheng's Continued Record of Examining Antiquity to expose the false slander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu's son Chongxian memorialized to clear his father's name. Lou asked that Zhao Shizhao be punished, Cai Lian's sentence reaffirmed, and Gong Yizheng's Continued Record of Examining Antiquity destroyed to expose the false charges.

sentences.zh: 除端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事，升同知，進參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Assistant Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, promoted to Vice Commissioner, and advanced to Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Duanming Hall academician and Assistant Commissioner of Military Affairs, promoted to Vice Commissioner, then Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 位兩府者五年，累疏求去，除資政殿學士、知太平州，辭，進大學士，提舉萬壽觀。

translations.literal: He held office in both councils for five years, repeatedly memorialized to resign, was appointed Academic Administrator of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Taiping Prefecture, declined, was advanced to Grand Academician, and appointed to administer the Wanshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He served in both councils for five years and repeatedly asked to retire. He was appointed Zizheng Hall academician and prefect of Taiping, declined, was advanced to Grand Academician, and appointed to administer Wanshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 嘉定六年薨，年七十七，贈少師，諡「宣獻」。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiading he died at age seventy-seven; he was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor and given the posthumous title "Xuancian."
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiading 6 (1213) at seventy-seven. He was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor with the posthumous title "Xuancian."

sentences.zh: 鑰文辭精博，自號「攻媿主人」，有集一百二十卷。

translations.literal: Yao's literary style was refined and encyclopedic; he styled himself "Master Gongkui" and left a collection of writings in one hundred twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Lou's prose was polished and learned. He styled himself "Master Gongkui" and left collected writings in 120 juan.

sentences.zh: 李大性

translations.literal: Li Daxing
translations.idiomatic: Li Daxing (section)

sentences.zh: 李大性，字伯和，端州四會人。

translations.literal: Li Daxing, styled Bohe, was a native of Sihui in Duan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daxing, courtesy name Bohe, came from Sihui in Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 其先積中，嘗為御史，以直言入元祐黨籍，始家豫章。

translations.literal: His ancestor Li Jizhong had once served as censor; for his outspoken remonstrance he was entered on the Yuanyou faction list, and the family first settled in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Li Jizhong had served as censor; for outspoken remonstrance he was listed among the Yuanyou faction, and the family first settled in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 大性少力學，尤習本朝典故。

translations.literal: Daxing from youth applied himself to learning and was especially versed in the institutions and precedents of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Daxing applied himself to study and was especially versed in Song institutional history.

sentences.zh: 以父任入官，因參選，進《藝祖廟謨》百篇及公私利害百疏。

translations.literal: Entering office through his father's privilege, he took part in selection and submitted one hundred chapters of Expositions on the Founder's Temple and one hundred memorials on public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through his father's privilege, participated in the selection process, and submitted one hundred chapters on the Founder's temple and one hundred memorials on public and private interests.

sentences.zh: 又言：「元豐制，六察許言事，章惇為相始禁之，乞復舊制，以廣言路。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Under the Yuanfeng system, the six investigating censors were permitted to speak on affairs; when Zhang Dun became chief councillor this was forbidden — I ask that the old system be restored to broaden the avenue of remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "Under the Yuanfeng system the six investigating censors could speak on state affairs; Zhang Dun as chief councillor forbade this. I ask that the old rule be restored to widen the path of remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 從臣力薦之，命赴都堂審察，僅遷一秩，為湖北提刑司幹官。

translations.literal: Following ministers strongly recommended him; he was ordered to undergo review at the Imperial Hall and was promoted only one rank, becoming administrative officer of the Hubei Circuit Intendant for Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers strongly recommended him. He was ordered to undergo review at the Imperial Hall and received only a one-rank promotion, becoming administrative officer of the Hubei Circuit Intendant for Punishments.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為主管吏部架閣文字。

translations.literal: Before long he entered service as supervisor of archival texts in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered service as supervisor of archival texts in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 丁母艱，服闋，進《典故辨疑》百篇，皆本朝故實，蓋網羅百氏野史，訂以日曆、實錄，核其正舛，率有據依，孝宗讀而褒嘉之。

translations.literal: When his mother's mourning ended and his mourning period was complete, he submitted one hundred chapters of Clarifying Doubts in Precedents — all facts of the dynasty, having gathered widely from unofficial histories of many schools, checked against the calendar and veritable records, and verified for accuracy and error, generally with solid basis; Emperor Xiaozong read them and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his mother, he submitted one hundred chapters of Clarifying Doubts in Precedents — dynastic facts drawn from hundreds of sources, checked against calendars and veritable records, and verified for accuracy. Xiaozong read them and commended him.

sentences.zh: 擢大理司直，遷敕令所刪定官，添差通判楚州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Directing Censor of the Court of Judicial Review, transferred to reviser at the Edicts and Ordinances Office, and given additional appointment as vice prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Directing Censor of the Court of Judicial Review, made a reviser at the Edicts and Ordinances Office, and given additional appointment as vice prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 郡守吳曦與都統劉超合議，欲撤城移他所，大性謂：「楚城實晉義烏間所築，最堅，奈何以脆薄易堅厚乎？」

translations.literal: The prefect Wu Xi and the regional commander Liu Chao jointly proposed withdrawing the city and relocating it elsewhere; Daxing said: "The walls of Chu were in fact built in the Jin between Yiwu counties — they are the sturdiest; how can one replace the firm and thick with the brittle and thin?"
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wu Xi and regional commander Liu Chao jointly proposed abandoning the city and relocating it. Daxing objected: "Chu's walls were built in the Jin period between Yiwu counties — they are exceptionally strong. How can we swap the solid for the flimsy?"

sentences.zh: 持不可。

translations.literal: He held firm and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 臺臣將劾其沮撓，不果。

translations.literal: Censorial officials were about to impeach him for obstruction, but did not carry it through.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials were about to impeach him for obstruction, but dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 會從官送北客，朝命因俾廉訪，具以實聞，遂罷戎帥，召大性除太府寺丞，遷大宗正丞兼倉部郎，尋改工部。

translations.literal: When attendant officials escorted northern guests, the court ordered him to conduct an inspection on that occasion and report the facts; the regional commander was then dismissed, and Daxing was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granary, promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan concurrently Director of the Granary Bureau, and soon transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When attendant officials escorted northern envoys, the court ordered him to investigate on that occasion and report truthfully. The regional commander was dismissed, Daxing was summoned, appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granary, then Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan with concurrent duty as Director of the Granary Bureau, and soon transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 陳傅良以言事去國，彭龜年、黃度、楊方相繼皆去。

translations.literal: Chen Fuliang left the capital for remonstrance; Peng Guinian, Huang Du, and Yang Fang left in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fuliang left the capital after remonstrating; Peng Guinian, Huang Du, and Yang Fang departed one after another.

sentences.zh: 大性抗疏言：「朝廷清明，乃使言者無故而去，臣所甚惜也。

translations.literal: Daxing submitted a forceful memorial, saying: "The court is clear and enlightened, yet remonstrators leave for no cause — this is what I deeply regret.
translations.idiomatic: Daxing submitted a forceful memorial: "The court is enlightened, yet remonstrators are driven out for no good reason — this grieves me deeply.

sentences.zh: 數人之心，皆本愛君，知其愛君，任其去而不顧，恐端人正士之去者將不止此。

translations.literal: The hearts of these several men all spring from love of the ruler; knowing they love the ruler, yet letting them go without concern — I fear upright men will not stop at this.
translations.idiomatic: These men all acted out of loyalty to the throne. Knowing their loyalty, yet letting them go without a second thought — I fear many more upright men will follow them out.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：『不信仁賢，則國空虛。』

translations.literal: Mencius said: 'If one does not trust the humane and worthy, the state will be left empty.'
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said: 'Without trust in the humane and worthy, the state is left hollow.'

sentences.zh: 臣所以為之寒心也。」

translations.literal: This is why I am chilled at heart."
translations.idiomatic: That is why this chills me to the core."

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，光宗疾，未能執喪。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong died, Guangzong was ill and unable to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong died, Guangzong was ill and unable to perform mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 大性復上疏言：「今日之事，顛倒舛逆，況金使祭奠當引見於北宮素帷，不知是時猶可以不出乎？

translations.literal: Daxing again submitted a memorial, saying: "Today's affairs are turned upside down and reversed; moreover, when the Jin envoy comes to offer condolences he should be received before the plain mourning canopy of the Northern Palace — can Your Majesty still fail to appear even then?
translations.idiomatic: Daxing memorialized again: "Matters today are inverted and perverse. When the Jin envoy arrives to offer condolences, he should be received before the plain mourning canopy in the Northern Palace — can Your Majesty still refuse to appear even then?

sentences.zh: 《檀弓》曰：『成人有兄死而不喪者，聞子皐將為成宰，遂為衰。

translations.literal: The Tann Gong says: Among the Cheng there was one whose elder brother had died yet who did not observe mourning; when he heard that Zigao was to become minister of Cheng, he then put on hemp mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The Tann Gong records that in Cheng there was a man whose brother had died but who wore no mourning — until he heard Zigao was to become minister of Cheng, whereupon he donned hemp mourning.

sentences.zh: 成人曰：「兄則死而子皐為之衰。」』

translations.literal: The man of Cheng said: "My brother is dead, yet Zigao wears mourning for him."
translations.idiomatic: The man of Cheng said: "My brother is dead, yet it is Zigao who wears mourning for him."

sentences.zh: 蓋言成人畏子皐之來方為制服，其服子皐為之，非為兄也。

translations.literal: This means the man of Cheng feared Zigao's coming and only then put on mourning garments; the mourning was done for Zigao, not for his brother.
translations.idiomatic: The point is that the man of Cheng feared Zigao's arrival and only then assumed mourning — the mourning was for Zigao's sake, not his brother's.

sentences.zh: 若陛下必待使來然後執喪，則恐貽譏中外，豈特如成人而已哉。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must wait until the envoy arrives before observing mourning, I fear ridicule at home and abroad — would it be limited to the man of Cheng alone?"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists on waiting for the envoy before performing mourning, I fear mockery at home and abroad — and not only from the man of Cheng."

sentences.zh: 遷軍器少監，權司封郎，提舉浙東常平，改浙東提刑兼知慶元府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Armory, acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel's Seals Bureau, appointed to administer Eastern Zhejiang Ever-Normal Granaries, and changed to Eastern Zhejiang Intendant for Punishments concurrently prefect of Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Armory, acting Director of the Seals Bureau, put in charge of Eastern Zhejiang Ever-Normal Granaries, then Eastern Zhejiang Intendant for Punishments with concurrent appointment as prefect of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 召為吏部郎中，四遷為司農卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and after four promotions became Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and, after four promotions, became Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 明年，兼戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year he concurrently served as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he also served as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 出知紹興府，甫一歲，召為戶部侍郎，升尚書。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Shaoxing, after only one year he was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue and promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed prefect of Shaoxing, he was recalled after only one year as Vice Minister of Revenue and then promoted to Minister.

sentences.zh: 朝論將用兵，大性條陳利害，主不宜輕舉之說，忤韓侂胄意，出知平江，移知福州，又移知江陵，充荊湖制置使。

translations.literal: Court opinion favored military action; Daxing itemized advantages and disadvantages, maintaining that rash action was inadvisable, offending Han Tuozhou's intent; he was sent out as prefect of Pingjiang, transferred to Fuzhou, then to Jiangling, and appointed Military Commissioner of Jinghu.
translations.idiomatic: With court opinion turning toward war, Daxing laid out pros and cons and argued against rash action, offending Han Tuozhou. He was sent to Pingjiang, then Fuzhou, then Jiangling as Military Commissioner of Jinghu.

sentences.zh: 江陵當用兵後，殘毀饑饉，繼以疾疫，大性首議振貸，凡三十八萬緡有奇。

translations.literal: Jiangling lay in the aftermath of war — ruined, famine-stricken, and then afflicted by pestilence; Daxing took the lead in proposing relief loans totaling more than three hundred eighty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling had been ravaged by war, famine, and plague in succession. Daxing led the push for relief loans totaling over 380,000 strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 前官虛羨，凡十有四萬五千緡，率蠲放不督，民流移新復業者，皆奏免征榷。

translations.literal: The previous official had inflated surplus accounts by one hundred forty-five thousand strings; he generally remitted and did not collect them; for people who had fled and newly returned to their occupations, he memorialized to exempt commercial taxes.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor had inflated surpluses by 145,000 strings; Daxing remitted these without collection. For refugees newly returned to work, he petitioned to waive commercial taxes.

sentences.zh: 邊郡武爵，本以勵士，冒濫滋眾，大性劾兩路戎司冒受逃亡付身，凡三千四百九十有七道，率繳上毀抹，左選為之一清。

translations.literal: Military ranks on the frontier were originally meant to encourage soldiers, but fraudulent appointments grew numerous; Daxing impeached the military commissioners of both routes for falsely accepting desertion transfer documents — three thousand four hundred ninety-seven in all — and had them all submitted and destroyed; irregular appointments were thereby cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier military ranks were meant to reward merit, but abuse proliferated. Daxing impeached both route military commissioners for falsely accepting 3,497 desertion transfer documents and had them confiscated and destroyed, cleaning up irregular appointments.

sentences.zh: 江陵舊使銅鏹，錢重楮輕，民持貲入市，有終日不得一錢者。

translations.literal: Jiangling formerly used copper cash; the cash was heavy and paper money light, and people bringing goods to market sometimes could not obtain a single coin all day.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling had used copper cash, but with heavy coin and depreciated paper notes, merchants sometimes spent a whole day at market without earning a single coin.

sentences.zh: 大性奏乞依襄、郢例通用鐵錢，於是泉貨流通，民始復業。

translations.literal: Daxing memorialized asking that iron cash be used in common, following the examples of Xiang and Ying; thereupon currency circulated and the people began to resume their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Daxing petitioned to adopt iron cash as in Xiangzhou and Yingzhou. Currency began to circulate again and people returned to their trades.

sentences.zh: 除刑部尚書兼詳定敕令，尋遷兵部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Justice concurrently reviser of edicts and ordinances, and soon transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Justice with concurrent duty revising edicts and ordinances, then transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 時金國分裂，不能自存，有舉北伐之議者，大性上疏以和戰之說未定，乞令朝臣集議，從之。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin state was splitting and could not sustain itself; some proposed a northern expedition; Daxing submitted a memorial that the debate over peace and war was unsettled and asked that court officials gather to deliberate — this was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was fracturing and could barely survive; some urged a northern campaign. Daxing memorialized that peace and war remained undecided and asked for a court conference — which was granted.

sentences.zh: 尋以端明殿學士知平江府，引疾丐祠，卒於家，年七十七，贈開府儀同三司，諡「文惠」。

translations.literal: Soon, as Academician of the Duanming Hall, he was made prefect of Pingjiang; citing illness he requested a sinecure and died at home at age seventy-seven; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Palace and given the posthumous title "Wenhui."
translations.idiomatic: Soon, as Duanming Hall academician and prefect of Pingjiang, he cited illness, requested a sinecure, and died at home at seventy-seven. He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the posthumous title "Wenhui."

sentences.zh: 李氏自積中三世官於朝，父子兄弟相師友，而大性與弟大異、大東並躋從列，為名臣云。

translations.literal: The Li family from Jizhong onward for three generations served at court; fathers, sons, and brothers taught and learned from one another; Daxing with his younger brothers Dayi and Dadong all reached the highest ranks — they were called eminent ministers.
translations.idiomatic: From Jizhong's generation the Li family served at court for three generations, fathers and sons learning from one another. Daxing and his brothers Dayi and Dadong all reached high office and were reckoned eminent ministers.

sentences.zh: 任希夷

translations.literal: Ren Xiyi
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xiyi (section)

sentences.zh: 任希夷，字伯起，其先眉州人。

translations.literal: Ren Xiyi, styled Boqi, was originally from Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xiyi, courtesy name Boqi, was originally from Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 四世祖伯雨為諫議大夫，其後仕閩，因家邵武。

translations.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor Boyu was Remonstrance and Critic; afterward the family served in Min and settled in Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: His fourth-generation ancestor Boyu was Remonstrance and Critic; later generations served in Min and settled in Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 希夷少刻意問學，為文精苦。

translations.literal: Xiyi from youth applied himself zealously to learning; his writing was refined and painstaking.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xiyi applied himself zealously to learning; his writing was painstaking and polished.

sentences.zh: 登淳熙三年進士第，調建寧府浦城簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Chunxi and was assigned as recorder of Pucheng in Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Chunxi 3 (1176) and was appointed recorder of Pucheng in Jianning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從朱熹學，篤信力行，熹器之曰：「伯起，開濟士也。」

translations.literal: He studied under Zhu Xi, believing firmly and acting resolutely; Xi valued him, saying: "Boqi is a man who can open paths and bring relief."
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Zhu Xi, believing and practicing with conviction. Xi prized him, saying: "Boqi is a man who can open paths and bring relief."

sentences.zh: 開禧初，主太常寺簿，奏：「紹熙以來，禮書未經編次，歲月滋久，恐或散亡，乞下本寺修纂。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaixi he served as chief clerk of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and memorialized: "Since Shaoxi, the ritual books have not been compiled and arranged; as years pass I fear they may be scattered and lost — I ask that this office be ordered to compile them."
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaixi he was chief clerk of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and memorialized: "Since Shaoxi the ritual codes have gone uncompiled; with time they may be lost. I ask that this office be ordered to compile them."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His request was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書兼給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites concurrently Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Rites, concurrently Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 謂：「周惇頤、程顥、程頤為百代絕學之倡，乞定議賜諡。」

translations.literal: He said: "Zhou Dunyi, Cheng Hao, and Cheng Yi were champions of learning unmatched for a hundred generations — I ask that posthumous titles be fixed and granted."
translations.idiomatic: He argued: "Zhou Dunyi, Cheng Hao, and Cheng Yi revived learning for the ages — I ask that their posthumous titles be formally granted."

sentences.zh: 其後惇頤諡「元」，顥諡「純」，頤諡「正」，皆希夷發之。

translations.literal: Thereafter Dunyi was given the posthumous title "Yuan," Hao "Chun," and Yi "Zheng" — all initiated by Xiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Dunyi was then given the posthumous title "Yuan," Hao "Chun," and Yi "Zheng" — all at Xiyi's initiative.

sentences.zh: 進端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Duanming Hall, Assistant Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and concurrently acting Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Duanming Hall academician, Assistant Commissioner of Military Affairs, and acting Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 史彌遠柄國久，執政皆具員，議者頗譏其拱默。

translations.literal: Shi Miyuan had long held power; the administration was fully staffed, and critics widely mocked their silence and inaction.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan had held power for years; the administration was fully staffed, and critics mocked their passivity.

sentences.zh: 尋提舉臨安洞霄宮，薨，贈少師，諡「宣獻」。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed to administer the Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an and died; he was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor and given the posthumous title "Xuancian."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed to administer the Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an and died. He was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor with the posthumous title "Xuancian."

sentences.zh: 徐應龍

translations.literal: Xu Yinglong
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yinglong (section)

sentences.zh: 徐應龍，字允叔。

translations.literal: Xu Yinglong, styled Yuncshu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yinglong, courtesy name Yuncshu.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年第進士，調衡州法曹、湖南檢法官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunxi he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as legal officer of Hengzhou and reviewing judge of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Chunxi 2 (1175) and was assigned as legal officer of Hengzhou and reviewing judge of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 潭獲劫盜，首謀者已繫獄，妄指逸者為首，吏信之，及獲逸盜，治之急，遂誣服。

translations.literal: In Tanzhou bandits were captured; the ringleader was already imprisoned but falsely named an escaped man as leader; the clerks believed it, and when the escaped bandit was caught he was prosecuted urgently and falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: In Tanzhou bandits were captured. The ringleader was already in custody but falsely named an escaped accomplice as leader. The clerks believed him; when the fugitive was caught he was pressed hard and falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 吏以成憲讞於憲司，應龍閱實其辭，謂：「首從不明，法當奏。」

translations.literal: The clerks, following established precedent, submitted the verdict to the judicial intendant; Yinglong examined the testimony and said: "Leader and follower are unclear — by law this should be reported to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Following precedent the clerks submitted the verdict to the intendant. Yinglong reviewed the testimony and said: "The roles of leader and follower are unclear — by law this must be reported upward."

sentences.zh: 時周必大判潭州，提刑盧彥德不欲反其事，將置逸盜於死，應龍力與之辨。

translations.literal: At the time Zhou Bida was prefect of Tanzhou; Intendant Lu Yande did not wish to reverse the case and was about to execute the escaped bandit; Yinglong forcefully argued with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bida was then prefect of Tanzhou; Intendant Lu Yande refused to reverse the case and was about to execute the fugitive. Yinglong argued forcefully against him.

sentences.zh: 先是，彥德許應龍京削，至是怒曰：「君不欲出我門邪？」

translations.literal: Earlier Yande had promised Yinglong a capital appointment; now he angrily said: "Do you not wish to leave through my door?"
translations.idiomatic: Yande had earlier promised Yinglong a capital appointment. Now he angrily said: "Do you not wish to advance through my patronage?"

sentences.zh: 應龍曰：「以人命傅文字，所不忍也。」

translations.literal: Yinglong said: "To attach a human life to written words — that I cannot bear."
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong replied: "I cannot bear to trade a man's life for a written verdict."

sentences.zh: 彥德不能奪，聞者多其有守，交薦之。

translations.literal: Yande could not override him; those who heard of it mostly praised his integrity, and many jointly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yande could not prevail. Word spread of his integrity, and many recommended him.

sentences.zh: 改秩，知瑞州高安縣。

translations.literal: His rank was changed; he was made magistrate of Gao'an County in Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He received a rank change and was appointed magistrate of Gao'an in Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 呂祖儉言事忤韓侂胄，謫死高安，應龍為之經紀其喪，且為文誄之。

translations.literal: Lü Zujian remonstrated on policy, offended Han Tuozhou, and was banished to die at Gao'an; Yinglong managed his funeral and also composed a eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zujian remonstrated, offended Han Tuozhou, and was banished to die at Gao'an. Yinglong arranged his funeral and wrote a eulogy.

sentences.zh: 有勸之避禍者，應龍曰：「呂君吾所敬，雖緣此獲譴，亦所願也。」

translations.literal: Some advised him to avoid disaster; Yinglong said: "Master Lü is one I respect; even if I suffer punishment for this, it is what I wish."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to avoid trouble. Yinglong said: "Master Lü is a man I revere. Even if I am punished for this, I accept it willingly."

sentences.zh: 朱熹貽書應龍曰：「高安之政，義風凜然。」

translations.literal: Zhu Xi wrote to Yinglong: "The governance of Gao'an — its moral spirit is awe-inspiring."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi wrote to him: "The moral authority of Gao'an's governance is formidable."

sentences.zh: 主淮西機宜文字，知南恩州。

translations.literal: He served as staff officer for Huaixi military affairs and was made prefect of Nan'en Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer for Huaixi military affairs and was appointed prefect of Nan'en.

sentences.zh: 陳自強當國，乃舊同舍，應龍丐雷州而去。

translations.literal: When Chen Ziqiang held power — an old fellow student — Yinglong requested Leizhou and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Ziqiang came to power — a former fellow student — Yinglong asked to be sent to Leizhou and departed.

sentences.zh: 召監都進奏院，遷國子博士、守工部員外郎，進戶部侍郎，遷國子司業兼實錄院檢討官、崇政殿說書、守秘書少監兼權工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as director of the Palace Memorial Reception Office, promoted to Doctor of the Directorate of Education and acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, advanced to Vice Minister of Revenue, transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education concurrently Veritable Records reviser, Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, and acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Works as Acting Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director of the Palace Memorial Reception Office, promoted to Doctor of the Directorate of Education and acting Vice Director of Works, advanced to Vice Minister of Revenue, then Vice Director of Education with concurrent posts as Veritable Records reviser, Chongzheng Hall lecturer, and acting Vice Director of Works as Acting Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 時金主徙汴，應龍言：「金人窮而南奔，將溢出而蹈吾之境。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin ruler moved to Bian; Yinglong said: "The Jurchens, driven to desperation, flee south and will overflow and tread upon our borders.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin ruler moved to Kaifeng, Yinglong warned: "The Jurchens, driven to desperation, are fleeing south and will spill over our borders.

sentences.zh: 金亡，更生新敵，尤為可慮。」

translations.literal: When Jin perishes, new enemies will arise — this is especially to be feared."
translations.idiomatic: When Jin falls, new enemies will arise — that is the greater worry."

sentences.zh: 兼侍講，言：「人主不能盡知天下人材，當責之宰相；

translations.literal: Concurrently Attendant Lecturer, he said: "The ruler cannot fully know all talent under heaven — this responsibility should be placed on the chief councillor;
translations.idiomatic: As Attendant Lecturer he said: "A ruler cannot know every talented man in the empire — that duty belongs to the chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 宰相不能盡知天下人材，當采之公論。

translations.literal: the chief councillor cannot fully know all talent under heaven — this should be drawn from public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: A chief councillor cannot know them all either — talent must be sought through public consensus.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫為相，號稱得人，而三人之薦，乃出於裴垍之疏。」

translations.literal: Li Jifu as chief councillor was said to have chosen men well, yet three men's recommendations came from Pei Ji's memorial alone."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu as chief councillor was praised for choosing men well, yet three of his appointments came from a single memorial by Pei Ji alone."

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，進刑部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and advanced to Minister of Punishments concurrently Attendant Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and promoted to Minister of Punishments with concurrent service as Attendant Reader.

sentences.zh: 應龍在講筵，多指陳時政。

translations.literal: At the lecture hall Yinglong frequently pointed out and discussed current policy.
translations.idiomatic: In the lecture hall Yinglong frequently addressed current policy.

sentences.zh: 一日讀吳起為卒吮疽事，應龍奏：「起恤士卒如此，故能得其死力。

translations.literal: One day, reading the story of Wu Qi sucking a soldier's abscess, Yinglong memorialized: "Qi cared for his troops thus and therefore could obtain their utmost effort.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while reading how Wu Qi sucked a soldier's abscess, Yinglong memorialized: "Wu Qi cared for his troops like this and so won their utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今軍將得以賄遷，專事掊克，未免多怨。」

translations.literal: Today military commanders can obtain transfers through bribes and devote themselves to extortion — resentment is unavoidable."
translations.idiomatic: Today commanders buy promotions with bribes and devote themselves to extortion — no wonder there is so much resentment."

sentences.zh: 上驚曰：「債帥之風，今猶未除邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said in alarm: "The wind of debt-commanders — is it still not eradicated today?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in alarm: "The wind of debt-commanders — has it still not been eradicated?"

sentences.zh: 宰相史彌遠聞而惡之，免侍讀。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan heard of it and resented him, and removed him as Attendant Reader.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan heard of it, took offense, and removed him as Attendant Reader.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼太子詹事。

translations.literal: Before long he was made concurrent Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 會景獻太子薨，請老，上不許，徙吏部尚書，以煥章閣學士提舉嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: When the Jingxian Heir Apparent died, he requested retirement; the emperor did not permit it and transferred him to Minister of Personnel, appointing him as Academician of the Huanzhang Hall to administer the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingxian Heir Apparent died, he asked to retire. The emperor refused and transferred him to Minister of Personnel, then appointed him Huanzhang Hall academician to administer Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十七年卒，贈開府儀同三司，諡「文肅」。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Jiading he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the posthumous title "Wensu."
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiading 17 (1224). He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the posthumous title "Wensu."

sentences.zh: 子：榮叟，官至參知政事，諡「文靖」；

translations.literal: Sons: Rongshou, who reached Vice Grand Councillor and was given the posthumous title "Wenjing";
translations.idiomatic: His sons: Rongshou, who rose to Vice Grand Councillor with the posthumous title "Wenjing";

sentences.zh: 深叟，官終將作監丞；

translations.literal: Shenshou, who ended as Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings;
translations.idiomatic: Shenshou ended as Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 清叟，知樞密院事兼參知政事。

translations.literal: Qingshou, who served as Commissioner of Military Affairs concurrently Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: and Qingshou, Commissioner of Military Affairs concurrently Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 各有傳。

translations.literal: Each has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Each has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 莊夏，字子禮，泉州人。

translations.literal: Zhuang Xia, styled Zili, was a native of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Xia, courtesy name Zili, came from Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳熙八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Chunxi 8 (1181).

sentences.zh: 慶元六年，大旱，詔求言。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qingyuan there was great drought; an edict sought remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingyuan 6 (1200) a severe drought prompted an edict soliciting remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 夏時知贛州興國縣，上封事曰：「君者陽也，臣者君之陰也。

translations.literal: Xia was then magistrate of Xingguo County in Ganzhou; he submitted a sealed memorial saying: "The ruler is yang; ministers are the ruler's yin.
translations.idiomatic: Xia was then magistrate of Xingguo in Ganzhou and submitted a sealed memorial: "The ruler is yang; ministers are his yin.

sentences.zh: 今威福下移，此陰勝也。

translations.literal: Now authority and favor shift downward — this is yin overcoming yang.
translations.idiomatic: When power and favor shift downward, yin overcomes yang.

sentences.zh: 積陰之極，陽氣散亂而不收，其弊為火災，為旱蝗。

translations.literal: When yin accumulates to the extreme, yang disperses in disorder and cannot be gathered; its evils are fire disasters, drought, and locusts.
translations.idiomatic: When yin accumulates to excess, yang scatters and cannot be reined in — the result is fire, drought, and locusts.

sentences.zh: 願陛下體陽剛之德，使後宮戚里、內省黃門，思不出位，此抑陰助陽之術也。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will embody the virtue of yang's firmness, causing the inner palace, imperial kin, and inner attendants to keep their thoughts within their proper bounds — this is the method of restraining yin and assisting yang."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will embody yang's firm strength, so that the inner palace, imperial relatives, and inner attendants keep their ambitions within bounds — that is how to restrain yin and strengthen yang."

sentences.zh: 召為太學博士。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Doctor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Doctor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 言：「比年分藩持節，詔墨未乾而改除，坐席未溫而易地，一人而歲三易節，一歲而郡四易守，民力何由裕？」

translations.literal: He said: "In recent years when princes hold regional commissions, the edict ink is not dry before a new appointment arrives; the seat is not warm before the place changes — one man changes his commission three times in a year, and one prefecture changes its prefect four times in a year; how can the people's strength be ample?"
translations.idiomatic: He said: "In recent years princes receive regional commissions only to be reassigned before the ink is dry. One man may change posts three times in a year; one prefecture may see four prefects in a year. How can the people's resources keep up?"

sentences.zh: 遷國子博士，召除吏部員外郎，遷軍器監，太府少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Doctor of the Directorate of Education, summoned and appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to Director of the Directorate of Armaments and Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He became Doctor of the Directorate of Education, was summoned as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then Director of Armaments and Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granary.

sentences.zh: 出知漳州，為宗正少卿兼國史院編修官，尋權直學士院兼太子侍讀。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Zhangzhou, he served as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan concurrently reviser of the National History Office, and soon concurrently acting member of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and Attendant Reader to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as prefect of Zhangzhou, he served as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and National History reviser, then concurrently acting Hanlin academician and Attendant Reader to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 時流民來歸，夏言：「荊襄、兩淮多不耕之田，計口授地，貸以屋廬牛具。

translations.literal: At the time refugees were returning; Xia said: "In Jingxiang and the two Huai regions there is much uncultivated land — allot fields by headcount and lend houses, oxen, and tools.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees were returning home. Xia said: "Jingxiang and the two Huai regions have much fallow land. Allot fields by headcount and lend housing, oxen, and tools.

sentences.zh: 吾乘其始至，可以得其欲；

translations.literal: If we seize their first arrival, we can obtain what they desire;
translations.idiomatic: If we act while they first arrive, we can give them what they need.

sentences.zh: 彼幸其不死，可以忘其勞。

translations.literal: when they rejoice at survival, they can forget their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful to be alive, they will forget their hardships.

sentences.zh: 兵民可合，屯田可成，此萬世一時也。」

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians can be combined, garrison fields can be established — this is a once-in-ten-thousand-generations opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians can be combined and garrison colonies established — a once-in-an-age opportunity."

sentences.zh: 試中書舍人兼太子右庶子、左諭德，言：「今戰守不成，而規模不定，則和好之說，得以乘間而入。

translations.literal: He passed the drafting secretary examination concurrently Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household and Left Preceptor, and said: "Now if war and defense are not settled and plans are not fixed, talk of peace can slip in through the gap.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the drafting secretary examination, concurrently Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household and Left Preceptor, and said: "With neither war nor defense settled and no clear strategy fixed, peace talk will find its opening.

sentences.zh: 今日之患，莫大於兵冗。

translations.literal: Today's evil is nowhere greater than redundant troops.
translations.idiomatic: Today's greatest ill is military bloat.

sentences.zh: 乞行下將帥，令老弱自陳，得以子若弟侄若婿強壯及等者收刺之，代其名糧。」

translations.literal: I ask that orders be sent to generals to let the old and weak declare themselves, so that sons, younger brothers, nephews, sons-in-law, or others of equal strength may be enlisted in their place, taking over their registered rations."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that generals be ordered to let the old and weak step forward, so sons, brothers, nephews, sons-in-law, or others of equal strength may be enlisted in their place and take over their rations."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「兵卒子弟與召募百姓不同，卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Soldiers' sons differ from recruited commoners — your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Soldiers' sons are not like recruited commoners — you are right."

sentences.zh: 除兵部侍郎、煥章閣待制，與祠歸。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of War and Attendant of the Huanzhang Pavilion, given a sinecure, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of War and Huanzhang Pavilion attendant, given a sinecure, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十年卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiading he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiading 10 (1217).

sentences.zh: 王阮，字南卿，江州人。

translations.literal: Wang Ruan, styled Nanqing, was a native of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ruan, courtesy name Nanqing, came from Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖韶，神宗時，開熙河，擒木征；

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shao, in Emperor Shenzong's time, opened the Hehuang region and captured Muzheng;
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shao, under Emperor Shenzong, opened the Hehuang region and captured Muzheng;

sentences.zh: 祖厚，繼辟湟、鄯；

translations.literal: His grandfather Hou continued to open Huang and Shan;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hou in turn opened Huang and Shan;

sentences.zh: 父彥傅，靖康勤王：皆有功。

translations.literal: his father Yanfu, in the Jingkang crisis, rallied troops to the emperor's aid — all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: his father Yanfu rallied troops to the emperor's aid during the Jingkang crisis — all distinguished themselves.

sentences.zh: 阮少好學，尚氣節。

translations.literal: Ruan from youth loved learning and valued integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ruan loved learning and prized integrity.

sentences.zh: 常自稱將種，辭辯奮發，四坐莫能屈。

translations.literal: He often called himself of military stock; in debate he was spirited and none present could refute him.
translations.idiomatic: He often called himself military stock; in debate he was fierce and no one in the room could best him.

sentences.zh: 嘗謁袁州太守張栻，栻謂曰：「當今道在武夷，子盍往求之。」

translations.literal: Once he visited Prefect Zhang Shi of Yuanzhou; Shi told him: "Today the Way is at Wuyi — why do you not go seek it?"
translations.idiomatic: Once he visited Prefect Zhang Shi of Yuanzhou. Shi told him: "The Way is at Wuyi today — why not go seek it there?"

sentences.zh: 阮見朱熹於考亭，熹與語，大說之。

translations.literal: Ruan visited Zhu Xi at Kaoting; Xi conversed with him and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan visited Zhu Xi at Kaoting. Xi spoke with him and was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 登隆興元年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Longxing 1 (1163).

sentences.zh: 時孝宗初即位，欲成高宗之志，首詔經理建業以圖進取，而大臣巽懦幸安，計未決。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xiaozong had just ascended the throne and wished to fulfill Emperor Gaozong's intent; he first issued an edict to manage Jianye to plan recovery, but the great ministers were timid and content with peace, and the plan was undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong had just ascended and wished to fulfill Gaozong's intent to recover the north. He first ordered preparations at Jianye, but timid ministers clinging to peace could not decide.

sentences.zh: 阮試禮部，對策曰：

translations.literal: Ruan tested at the Ministry of Rites and in his policy response said:
translations.idiomatic: In the Ministry of Rites examination Ruan wrote in his policy response:

sentences.zh: 「臨安蟠幽宅阻，面湖背海，膏腴沃野，足以休養生聚，其地利於休息。

translations.literal: "Lin'an lies coiled in secluded, obstructed terrain, facing the lake with the sea at its back; its fertile fields are sufficient to rest and gather the people — its terrain favors rest.
translations.idiomatic: "Lin'an nestles in secluded, obstructed terrain, lake to the front and sea behind; its fertile fields suffice to rest and gather the people — its terrain favors repose.

sentences.zh: 建康東南重鎮，控制長江呼吸之間，上下千里，足以虎視吳、楚，應接梁、宋，其地利於進取。

translations.literal: Jianye is the great stronghold of the southeast, controlling the Yangzi within a breath's span; for a thousand li up and down it suffices to look down on Wu and Chu and connect with Liang and Song — its terrain favors advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jianye is the southeast's great stronghold, commanding the Yangzi at its narrow waist. For a thousand li up and down it dominates Wu and Chu and links Liang and Song — its terrain favors advance.

sentences.zh: 建炎、紹興間，敵人乘勝長驅直搗，而我師亦甚憊也。

translations.literal: Between Jianyan and Shaoxing the enemy, riding victory, drove straight in, and our armies were also very weary.
translations.idiomatic: Between Jianyan and Shaoxing the enemy rode their victories straight south while our armies were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 上皇遵養時晦，不得與平，迺駐臨安，所以為休息計也。

translations.literal: The retired emperor nourished his strength and bided his time, unable to contend for peace, and therefore halted at Lin'an — this was a plan for rest.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor bided his time, unable yet to contest for peace, and halted at Lin'an — a plan for rest.

sentences.zh: 已三十年來，闕者全，壞者修，弊者整，廢者復，較以曩昔，倍萬不侔。

translations.literal: Already thirty years have passed; what was missing is complete, what was broken is repaired, what was worn is put in order, what was abandoned is restored — compared with former times, it is ten thousand times greater.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years have passed; gaps are filled, ruins repaired, decay restored, abandonment revived — compared with the past, the realm is incomparably stronger.

sentences.zh: 主上獨見遠覽，舉而措諸事業，非固以臨安為不足居也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty alone sees far; raising this and applying it to enterprise — it is not that Lin'an is inherently unfit to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty sees further than others. To raise this plan is not to say Lin'an is unfit to dwell in.

sentences.zh: 戰守之形既分，動靜進退之理異也。

translations.literal: Once the forms of war and defense are divided, the principles of movement, stillness, advance, and retreat differ.
translations.idiomatic: Once war and defense take separate forms, the logic of movement, stillness, advance, and retreat changes.

sentences.zh: 古者立國，必有所恃，謀國之要，必負其所恃之地。

translations.literal: In antiquity in establishing a state one must have something to rely on; the essential of planning for the state must lean on the place one relies upon.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient states rested on something they could rely upon; national strategy must lean on that foundation.

sentences.zh: 秦有函谷，蜀有劍閣，魏有成皐，趙有井陘，燕有飛狐，而吳有長江，皆其所恃以為國也。

translations.literal: Qin had Hangu Pass, Shu had Sword Gate, Wei had Chenggao, Zhao had Jingxing, Yan had Flying Fox, and Wu had the Yangzi — all relied on these to be states.
translations.idiomatic: Qin had Hangu Pass, Shu the Sword Gate, Wei Chenggao, Zhao Jingxing, Yan Flying Fox, and Wu the Yangzi — each relied on these strongpoints to endure.

sentences.zh: 今東南王氣，鍾在建業，長江千里，控扼所會，輟而弗顧，退守幽深之地，若將終身焉，如是而曰謀國，果得為善謀乎？

translations.literal: Now the kingly qi of the southeast concentrates at Jianye; the Yangzi for a thousand li is the choke point where control converges — to set it aside and not regard it, retreating to guard a deep and hidden place as if to end one's days there, and yet call this planning for the state — can this truly be called good planning?
translations.idiomatic: The southeast's royal qi gathers at Jianye. The thousand-li Yangzi is the strategic choke point — to ignore it, retreat to deep seclusion as if to end one's days there, and call that statecraft — is that wise planning?

sentences.zh: 且夫戰者以地為本，湖山回環，孰與乎龍盤虎踞之雄？

translations.literal: Moreover, in war land is fundamental; lakes and mountains winding around — how do they compare with the majesty of the dragon coiled and tiger crouched?
translations.idiomatic: War rests on terrain. Winding lakes and hills — how do they compare with the dragon-coiled, tiger-crouched majesty of Jianye?

sentences.zh: 胥潮奔猛，孰與乎長江之險？

translations.literal: The Qiantang bore rushes fiercely — how do they compare with the Yangzi's peril?
translations.idiomatic: The Qiantang bore rushes in fury — how does that compare with the Yangzi's natural barrier?

sentences.zh: 今議者徒習吳、越之僻固，而不知秣陵之通達，是猶富人之財，不布於通都大邑，而匣金以守之，愚恐半夜之或失也。

translations.literal: Today's debaters merely accustom themselves to Wu and Yue's narrow defensiveness and do not know Moling's openness and reach — this is like a rich man's wealth, not spread in great cities and markets but boxed in gold to guard it; I fear it may be lost in the middle of the night.
translations.idiomatic: Today's debaters cling to Wu and Yue's cramped defensiveness and ignore Moling's openness and reach — like a rich man hoarding gold in a box instead of deploying it in great markets; I fear it may be lost overnight.

sentences.zh: 儻六飛順動，中原在跬步間，況一建康耶？

translations.literal: If the imperial carriage moves accordingly, the Central Plain is within a short step — how much more so merely Jianye?
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial carriage moves accordingly, the Central Plain is a step away — to say nothing of Jianye alone.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：『千里之行，起於足下。』

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: 'A journey of a thousand li begins beneath the foot.'
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: 'A journey of a thousand li begins beneath one's foot.'

sentences.zh: 人患不為爾。」

translations.literal: The trouble is only that men do not act — that is all."
translations.idiomatic: The trouble is simply that men fail to act — nothing more."

sentences.zh: 知貢舉范成大得而讀之，歎曰：「是人傑也。」

translations.literal: Fan Chengda, chief examiner, obtained and read it and sighed: "This is a towering talent."
translations.idiomatic: Chief examiner Fan Chengda read it and exclaimed: "This is a towering talent."

sentences.zh: 調南康都昌主簿，以廉聲聞，移永州教授。

translations.literal: He was assigned as chief clerk of Duchang in Nankang and was known for integrity; he was transferred to professor at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned chief clerk of Duchang in Nankang, noted for integrity, then professor at Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 獻書闕下，請罷吳、楚牧馬之政，而積馬於蜀茶馬司，以省往來綱驛之費、歲時分牧之資，凡數千言。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial at court asking to abolish the Wu and Chu horse-pasturing policy and accumulate horses at the Sichuan Tea-Horse Office, to save the costs of courier stations in transit and seasonal pasturing — several thousand words in all.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial at court to abolish Wu and Chu horse pasturing and concentrate horses at the Sichuan Tea-Horse Office, saving courier and seasonal pasturing costs — several thousand words in all.

sentences.zh: 紹熙中，知濠州，請復曹瑋方田，修种世衡射法，日講守備，與邊民親訪北境事宜。

translations.literal: In Shaoxi he was made prefect of Haozhou; he asked to restore Cao Wei's square fields, repair Zhong Shihang's archery methods, daily discussed defense preparations, and with border people personally inquired into northern affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi he became prefect of Haozhou, restored Cao Wei's square-field system, revived Zhong Shihang's archery methods, drilled daily on defense, and personally consulted border people on northern affairs.

sentences.zh: 終阮在濠，金不敢南侵。

translations.literal: Throughout Ruan's tenure at Hao, Jin did not dare invade south.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Ruan's tenure at Hao, Jin did not dare raid south.

sentences.zh: 改知撫州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄宿聞阮名，特命入奏，將誘以美官，夜遣密客詣阮，阮不答，私謂所親曰：「吾聞公卿擇士，士亦擇公卿。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou had long heard of Ruan's name and specially ordered him to enter court and report; intending to lure him with fine office, at night he sent a secret agent to Ruan; Ruan did not reply and privately told those close to him: "I have heard that ministers and nobles choose scholars, and scholars also choose ministers and nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou had long heard of Ruan and ordered him to court, intending to lure him with high office. At night he sent a secret envoy; Ruan did not respond and told confidants: "Ministers choose scholars, and scholars choose ministers.

sentences.zh: 劉歆、柳宗元失身匪人，為萬世笑。

translations.literal: Liu Xin and Liu Zongyuan lost themselves to unworthy men and are laughed at for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin and Liu Zongyuan attached themselves to unworthy patrons and are mocked through the ages.

sentences.zh: 今政自韓氏出，吾肯出其門哉？」

translations.literal: Now power issues from the Han clan — would I be willing to come from their door?"
translations.idiomatic: Power now issues from the Han clan — would I serve under their banner?"

sentences.zh: 陛對畢，拂衣出關。

translations.literal: When the audience before the throne was finished, he brushed his robe and left through the pass.
translations.idiomatic: When his audience ended, he brushed off his robes and left through the pass.

sentences.zh: 侂胄聞之大怒，批旨予祠。

translations.literal: Tuozhou heard and was greatly angered; an annotated edict gave him a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was furious and issued an annotated edict granting him a sinecure.

sentences.zh: 阮於是歸隱廬山，盡棄人間事，從容觴詠而已。

translations.literal: Ruan then retired in seclusion on Mount Lu, abandoning all worldly affairs and contenting himself with leisurely wine and verse.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan then retired to Mount Lu, abandoning worldly affairs and contenting himself with wine and poetry.

sentences.zh: 朱熹嘗惜其才氣術略過人，而留滯不偶云。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi once regretted that his talent, energy, and strategic ability surpassed others, yet he remained blocked and unlucky.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi once lamented that Ruan's talent, energy, and strategic ability surpassed others, yet he remained blocked and unlucky.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiading 1 (1208).

sentences.zh: 王質，字景文，其先鄆州人，後徙興國。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi, styled Jingwen, was originally from Yun Prefecture and later moved to Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, courtesy name Jingwen, was originally from Yunzhou and later moved to Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 質博通經史，善屬文。

translations.literal: Zhi was broadly versed in the classics and histories and skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was broadly versed in classics and histories and skilled at prose.

sentences.zh: 遊太學，與九江王阮齊名。

translations.literal: Studying at the Imperial Academy, he was equally famous with Wang Ruan of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Academy he was as renowned as Wang Ruan of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 阮每云：「聽景文論古，如讀酈道元《水經》，名川支川，貫穿周匝，無有間斷，咳唾皆成珠璣。」

translations.literal: Ruan often said: "Listening to Jingwen discuss antiquity is like reading Li Daoyuan's Water Classic — famous rivers and branch streams run through and around without break; even his coughs and spittle become pearls."
translations.idiomatic: Ruan often said: "Listening to Jingwen discuss antiquity is like reading Li Daoyuan's Water Classic — main rivers and tributaries flow without interruption; even his casual words become pearls."

sentences.zh: 質與張孝祥父子遊，深見器重。

translations.literal: Zhi associated with Zhang Xiaoxiang and his son and was deeply valued.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi befriended Zhang Xiaoxiang and his son and was deeply valued by them.

sentences.zh: 孝祥為中書舍人，將薦質舉制科，會去國不果。

translations.literal: Xiaoxiang as Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat was about to recommend Zhi for the special decree examination, but left the capital and it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoxiang was Drafting Secretary he was about to recommend Zhi for the special decree examination, but left the capital before it could happen.

sentences.zh: 著論五十篇，言歷代君臣治亂，謂之《朴論》。

translations.literal: He composed fifty treatises on the governance and disorder of rulers and ministers through the ages, calling them the Plain Treatises.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote fifty treatises on rulers and ministers through the ages, called the Plain Treatises.

sentences.zh: 中紹興三十年進士第，用大臣言，召試館職，不就。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Shaoxing he passed the jinshi examination; on a great minister's recommendation he was summoned to test for an academy post but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 30 (1160) he passed the jinshi. On a minister's recommendation he was summoned to test for an academy post but declined.

sentences.zh: 明年，金主完顏亮南侵，御史中丞汪澈宣諭荊、襄，又明年，樞密使張浚都督江、淮，皆辟為屬。

translations.literal: The next year the Jin ruler Wanyan Liang invaded south; Censor-in-Chief Wang Che was dispatched to proclaim edicts in Jing and Xiang; the year after, Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Jun directed Jiang and Huai — all recruited him as staff.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wanyan Liang invaded south. Censor-in-Chief Wang Che was dispatched to Jing and Xiang; the year after, Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Jun directed Jiang and Huai — both recruited Zhi as staff.

sentences.zh: 入為太學正。

translations.literal: He entered service as Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 時孝宗屢易相，國論未定，質乃上疏曰：「陛下即位以來，慨然起乘時有為之志，而陳康伯、葉義問、汪澈在廷，陛下皆不以為才，於是先逐義問，次逐澈，獨徘徊康伯，難於進退，陛下意終鄙之，遂決意用史浩，而浩亦不稱陛下意，於是決用張浚，而浚又無成，於是決用湯思退。

translations.literal: At the time Xiaozong frequently changed chief councillors and national policy was unsettled; Zhi submitted a memorial saying: "Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, You have stirred with the ambition to seize the moment and act — yet with Chen Kangbo, Ye Yiwen, and Wang Che at court, Your Majesty deemed none of them capable. You first dismissed Yiwen, then Che, but hesitated over Kangbo, finding it hard to advance or retreat; Your Majesty ultimately came to despise him and resolved to use Shi Hao — yet Hao also did not suit Your Majesty's intent. Then You resolved to use Zhang Jun — yet Jun achieved nothing. Then You resolved to use Tang Situ.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong frequently changed chief councillors and national policy was unsettled. Zhi submitted a memorial: "Since Your Majesty took the throne, You have burned with ambition to seize the moment — yet with Chen Kangbo, Ye Yiwen, and Wang Che at court, You deemed none of them capable. You first dismissed Yiwen, then Che, but hesitated over Kangbo, unable to decide; You ultimately despised him and turned to Shi Hao — yet Hao also failed You.
