Then You turned to Zhang Jun — yet Jun achieved nothing. Then You turned to Tang Situ.

sentences.zh: 今思退專任國政，又且數月，臣度其終無益於陛下。

translations.literal: Now Situ monopolizes state affairs, and already for several months — your servant gauges that he will ultimately bring no benefit to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Now Situ monopolizes state affairs, and after several months I gauge that he will ultimately do Your Majesty no good.

sentences.zh: 夫宰相之任一不稱，則陛下之志一沮。

translations.literal: When a chief councillor's appointment fails in one respect, the emperor's intent is frustrated once.
translations.idiomatic: When a chief councillor fails in one respect, the emperor's intent is frustrated once.

sentences.zh: 前日康伯持陛下以和，和不成；

translations.literal: Earlier Kangbo held the emperor to peace — peace did not succeed;
translations.idiomatic: First Kangbo held the emperor to peace — peace failed.

sentences.zh: 浚持陛下以戰，戰不驗；

translations.literal: Jun held the emperor to war — war was not validated;
translations.idiomatic: Jun held him to war — war did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 浚又持陛下以守，守既困；

translations.literal: Jun again held the emperor to defense — defense was already strained;
translations.idiomatic: Jun again held him to defense — defense grew strained.

sentences.zh: 思退又持陛下以和。

translations.literal: Situ again held the emperor to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Situ again held him to peace.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦嘗深察和、戰、守之事乎？

translations.literal: Has Your Majesty also deeply examined the matters of peace, war, and defense?
translations.idiomatic: Has Your Majesty truly examined peace, war, and defense together?

sentences.zh: 李牧在雁門，法主於守，守乃有戰。

translations.literal: Li Mu at Yanmen took defense as fundamental — defense then made war possible.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu at Yanmen made defense fundamental — and defense made war possible.

sentences.zh: 祖逖在河南，法主於戰，戰乃有和。

translations.literal: Zu Ti in Henan took war as fundamental — war then made peace possible.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti in Henan made war fundamental — and war made peace possible.

sentences.zh: 羊祜在襄陽，法主於和，和乃有守。

translations.literal: Yang Hu at Xiangyang took peace as fundamental — peace then made defense possible.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu at Xiangyang made peace fundamental — and peace made defense possible.

sentences.zh: 何至分而不使相合？

translations.literal: Why must they be divided and not allowed to combine?
translations.idiomatic: Why divide them instead of combining them?

sentences.zh: 今陛下之心志未定，規模未立。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's resolve is unsettled and plans are not established.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's resolve is unsettled and no clear plan is fixed.

sentences.zh: 或告陛下，金弱且亡，而吾兵甚振，陛下則勃然有勒燕然之志；

translations.literal: If someone tells Your Majesty that Jin is weak and about to perish while our armies are very strong, Your Majesty suddenly swells with the ambition to inscribe Yanran;
translations.idiomatic: Tell him Jin is weak and dying while our armies are strong, and he suddenly burns with ambition to inscribe Yanran.

sentences.zh: 或告陛下，吾力不足恃，而金人且來，陛下即委然有盟平涼之心；

translations.literal: if someone tells Your Majesty that our strength cannot be relied upon and the Jurchens are coming, Your Majesty at once sinks into the mind to ally at Pingliang;
translations.idiomatic: Tell him our strength cannot be relied upon and the Jurchens are coming, and he sinks into thoughts of allying at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 或告陛下，吾不可進，金不可入，陛下又蹇然有指鴻溝之意。

translations.literal: if someone tells Your Majesty that we cannot advance and Jin cannot enter, Your Majesty again stiffly fixes on pointing at Honggou.
translations.idiomatic: Tell him we cannot advance and Jin cannot enter, and he stiffly fixes on the Honggou line.

sentences.zh: 使臣為陛下謀，會三者為一，天下烏有不治哉？」

translations.literal: If your servant plans for Your Majesty, uniting the three into one — would the empire not be governed?"
translations.idiomatic: If I may plan for Your Majesty: unite the three into one — would the empire not be governed?"

sentences.zh: 天子心知質忠，而忌者共讒質年少好異論，遂罷去。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven knew in his heart that Zhi was loyal, but those who envied him jointly slandered him as young and fond of strange opinions, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Zhi was loyal, but envious men slandered him as young and fond of eccentric views, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 會虞允文宣撫川、陝，辟質偕行。

translations.literal: When Yu Yunwen was dispatched to pacify Chuan and Shan, he recruited Zhi to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yunwen was dispatched to pacify Sichuan and Shaanxi, he recruited Zhi to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 一日令草檄契丹文，援毫立就，辭氣激壯。

translations.literal: One day he ordered him to draft a proclamation in Khitan; he took up the brush and finished at once — the language spirited and bold.
translations.idiomatic: One day he ordered a Khitan proclamation drafted; Zhi took up the brush and finished at once, the language bold and spirited.

sentences.zh: 允文起執其手曰：「景文天才也。」

translations.literal: Yunwen rose and took his hand, saying: "Jingwen is a genius."
translations.idiomatic: Yunwen rose, took his hand, and said: "Jingwen is a genius."

sentences.zh: 入為敕令所刪定官，遷樞密院編修官。

translations.literal: He entered service as reviser at the Edicts and Ordinances Office and was transferred to compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became a reviser at the Edicts and Ordinances Office and was transferred to compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 允文當國，孝宗命擬進諫官，允文以質鯁亮不回，且文學推重於時，可右正言。

translations.literal: When Yunwen held power, Xiaozong ordered recommendations for remonstrance officials; Yunwen, because Zhi was upright and unyielding and his literary learning was respected in the age, said he could serve as Right Remonstrance and Critic.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunwen held power, Xiaozong ordered remonstrance officials recommended. Yunwen said Zhi, upright and unyielding with literary standing respected in the age, could serve as Right Remonstrance and Critic.

sentences.zh: 時中貴人用事，多畏憚質，陰沮之，出通判荊南府，改吉州，皆不行，奉祠山居，絕意祿仕。

translations.literal: At the time eunuchs held power and many feared Zhi; they secretly obstructed him; he was sent out as vice prefect of Jingnan Prefecture, transferred to Jizhou — neither was accepted; he received a sinecure and lived in the mountains, utterly abandoning desire for office and salary.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs then held power and feared Zhi; they obstructed him secretly. He was sent out as vice prefect of Jingnan and transferred to Jizhou — he accepted neither and took a sinecure in the mountains, abandoning all desire for office.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十五年卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chunxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chunxi 15 (1188).

sentences.zh: 陸游字務觀，越州山陰人。

translations.literal: Lu You, styled Wuguan, was a native of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu You, courtesy name Wuguan, came from Shanyin in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 年十二能詩文，蔭補登仕郎。

translations.literal: At age twelve he could compose poetry and prose; by yin privilege he entered as Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he could write poetry and prose; by yin privilege he entered as Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement.

sentences.zh: 鎖廳薦送第一，秦檜孫塤適居其次，檜怒，至罪主司。

translations.literal: In the locked-hall recommended submission he ranked first; Qin Hui's grandson Kuan happened to rank second; Hui was angry and even punished the chief examiner.
translations.idiomatic: In the locked-hall examination he ranked first; Qin Hui's grandson Kuan ranked second. Hui was furious and even punished the chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 明年，試禮部，主司復置游前列，檜顯黜之，由是為所嫉。

translations.literal: The next year in the Ministry of Rites examination the chief examiner again placed You in the front ranks; Hui openly demoted him, and from this he was envied by Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The next year in the Ministry of Rites examination the chief examiner again placed You high; Hui openly demoted him, and from then on Hui envied him.

sentences.zh: 檜死，始赴福州寧德簿，以薦者除敕令所刪定官。

translations.literal: When Hui died, You at last went to Ningde as recorder in Fuzhou; on a recommender's nomination he was appointed reviser at the Edicts and Ordinances Office.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui's death You at last went to Ningde as recorder in Fuzhou; on recommendation he was appointed reviser at the Edicts and Ordinances Office.

sentences.zh: 時楊存中久掌禁旅，游力陳非便，上嘉其言，遂罷存中。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Cunzhong had long commanded the palace guard; You forcefully stated this was inadvisable; the emperor praised his words and Cunzhong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cunzhong had long commanded the palace guard. You argued forcefully that this was unwise; the emperor praised him and Cunzhong was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 中貴人有市北方珍玩以進者，游奏：「陛下以『損』名齋，自經籍翰墨外，屏而不御。

translations.literal: A eunuch purchased northern curios to present; You memorialized: "Your Majesty named your studio 'Diminishment' — apart from classics and brushwork, all is screened and not used.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch purchased northern curios for presentation. You memorialized: "Your Majesty named your studio 'Diminishment' — apart from classics and brushwork, all else is excluded.

sentences.zh: 小臣不體聖意，輒私買珍玩，虧損聖德，乞嚴行禁絕。」

translations.literal: Petty officials do not embody the sage's intent but privately buy curios — this damages sage virtue; I ask that prohibition be strictly enforced."
translations.idiomatic: Petty officials ignore the emperor's intent and privately buy curios — this damages imperial virtue. I ask that this be strictly forbidden."

sentences.zh: 應詔言：「非宗室外家，雖實有勳勞，毋得輒加王爵。

translations.literal: In response to an edict he said: "Apart from imperial clansmen and consort kin, even if they truly have merit, they must not rashly be given princely titles.
translations.idiomatic: Responding to an edict he said: "Apart from imperial clansmen and consort kin, even those with real merit must not rashly receive princely titles.

sentences.zh: 頃者有以師傅而領殿前都指揮使，復有以太尉而領閤門事，瀆亂名器，乞加訂正。」

translations.literal: Recently some who were tutors also commanded the Palace Front Command, and some who were Grand Preceptors also directed the Palace Gate Office — names and instruments are profaned; I ask for correction."
translations.idiomatic: Recently tutors have commanded the Palace Front Guard, and Grand Preceptors have directed the Palace Gate Office — titles are debased. I ask for correction."

sentences.zh: 遷大理寺司直兼宗正簿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Directing Censor of the Court of Judicial Review concurrently clerk of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Directing Censor of the Court of Judicial Review, concurrently clerk of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，遷樞密院編修官兼編類聖政所檢討官。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, he was transferred to compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs concurrently reviser at the Office for Compiling Sagely Governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended, he was transferred to compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, concurrently reviser at the Office for Compiling Sagely Governance.

sentences.zh: 史浩、黃祖舜薦游善詞章，諳典故，召見，上曰：「游力學有聞，言論剴切。」

translations.literal: Shi Hao and Huang Zushun recommended You for skill in composition and familiarity with precedents; he was summoned for audience; the emperor said: "You applies himself to learning with reputation; his speech is incisive."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hao and Huang Zushun recommended You for literary skill and knowledge of precedent. Summoned to audience, the emperor said: "You are known for diligent learning; your speech is incisive."

sentences.zh: 遂賜進士出身。

translations.literal: He was then granted jinshi status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon granted him jinshi status.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：「陛下初即位，乃信詔令以示人之時，而官吏將帥一切玩習，宜取其尤沮格者，與眾棄之。」

translations.literal: Entering for audience he said: "Your Majesty has just ascended — this is the time to make edicts trustworthy before the people, yet officials and generals treat everything as routine; take those who most obstruct and reject them before all."
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said: "Your Majesty has just ascended — this is the time to make edicts credible, yet officials and generals treat everything as routine. Punish the worst obstructors before all."

sentences.zh: 和議將成，游又以書白二府曰：「江左自吳以來，未有舍建康他都者。

translations.literal: When peace talks were about to succeed, You also wrote the two departments: "Since Wu in the Jiangzuo region, none has abandoned Jianye for another capital.
translations.idiomatic: As peace talks neared success, You wrote the two departments: "Since Wu ruled the southeast, no dynasty has abandoned Jianye for another capital.

sentences.zh: 駐蹕臨安出於權宜，形勢不固，饋餉不便，海道逼近，凜然意外之憂。

translations.literal: Halting at Lin'an was a measure of expediency; the situation is not firm, supplies are inconvenient, and the sea route draws near — there is a chill of unexpected worry.
translations.idiomatic: Halting at Lin'an was expedient; the position is insecure, logistics awkward, and the sea route dangerously close — inviting unexpected disaster.

sentences.zh: 一和之後，盟誓已立，動有拘礙。

translations.literal: Once peace is made, oaths are established and every move is constrained.
translations.idiomatic: Once peace is made, oaths bind us and every move is constrained.

sentences.zh: 今當與之約，建康、臨安皆係駐蹕之地，北使朝聘，或就建康，或就臨安，如此則我得以暇時建都立國，彼不我疑。」

translations.literal: Now we should agree with them that both Jianye and Lin'an are places of imperial residence; when northern envoys come on court visits they may go to Jianye or Lin'an — thus we can use idle time to establish a capital and state, and they will not suspect us."
translations.idiomatic: We should agree that both Jianye and Lin'an are imperial residences; northern envoys on court visits may go to either — thus we can use the interval to build a capital without arousing suspicion."

sentences.zh: 時龍大淵、曾覿用事，游為樞臣張燾言：「覿、大淵招權植黨，熒惑聖聽，公及今不言，異日將不可去。」

translations.literal: At the time Long Dayuan and Zeng Di held power; You told the military commissioner Zhang Jun: "Di and Dayuan gather power and build factions, deluding the sage's hearing — if you do not speak now, later they cannot be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Long Dayuan and Zeng Di held power. You told Military Commissioner Zhang Jun: "Di and Dayuan gather power and build factions, deluding the emperor — if you do not speak now, they cannot be removed later."

sentences.zh: 燾遽以聞，上詰語所自來，燾以游對。

translations.literal: Jun hastily reported this; the emperor interrogated where the words came from; Jun answered that they came from You.
translations.idiomatic: Jun hastily reported this. The emperor demanded the source; Jun named You.

sentences.zh: 上怒，出通判建康府，尋易隆興府。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; You was sent out as vice prefect of Jianye Prefecture and soon transferred to Longxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry. You was sent out as vice prefect of Jianye, then transferred to Longxing.

sentences.zh: 言者論游交結臺諫，鼓唱是非，力說張浚用兵，免歸。

translations.literal: Critics argued that You consorted with censors and remonstrators, stirring right and wrong, and forcefully urged Zhang Jun to use troops; he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged that You consorted with censors, stirred controversy, and forcefully urged Zhang Jun to war. He was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 久之，通判夔州。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made vice prefect of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made vice prefect of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 王炎宣撫川、陝，辟為幹辦公事。

translations.literal: Wang Yan was dispatched to pacify Chuan and Shan and recruited him as administrative officer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was dispatched to pacify Sichuan and Shaanxi and recruited him as administrative officer.

sentences.zh: 游為炎陳進取之策，以為經略中原必自長安始，取長安必自隴右始。

translations.literal: You presented Yan a strategy of advance, holding that to plan the Central Plain one must begin at Chang'an, and to take Chang'an one must begin at Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: You presented Yan a strategy of advance: to recover the Central Plain one must begin at Chang'an, and to take Chang'an one must begin at Longyou.

sentences.zh: 當積粟練兵，有釁則攻，無則守。

translations.literal: One should accumulate grain and drill troops — attack when there is an opening, defend when there is none.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulate grain and drill troops — attack when opportunity opens, defend when it does not.

sentences.zh: 吳璘子挺代掌兵，頗驕恣，傾財結士，屢以過誤殺人，炎莫誰何。

translations.literal: Wu Lin's son Ting took command of the army, quite arrogant and willful, spending wealth to win over scholars, repeatedly killing men through errors — Yan could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin's son Ting took command, arrogant and willful, spending wealth to win scholars and repeatedly killing men through negligence — Yan could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 游請以玠子拱代挺。

translations.literal: You asked that Jie's son Gong replace Ting.
translations.idiomatic: You asked that Wu Jie's son Gong replace Ting.

sentences.zh: 炎曰：「拱怯而寡謀，遇敵必敗。」

translations.literal: Yan said: "Gong is timid and lacks strategy; meeting the enemy he will surely be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said: "Gong is timid and lacks strategy; he will surely be defeated."

sentences.zh: 游曰：「使挺遇敵，安保其不敗。

translations.literal: You said: "If Ting meets the enemy, who guarantees he will not be defeated?
translations.idiomatic: You replied: "If Ting meets the enemy, who guarantees he will not be defeated?

sentences.zh: 就令有功，愈不可駕馭。」

translations.literal: Even if he had merit, he would be all the harder to control."
translations.idiomatic: Even if he won battles, he would be harder still to control."

sentences.zh: 及挺子曦僭叛，游言始驗。

translations.literal: When Ting's son Xi rebelled in usurpation, You's words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting's son Xi rebelled, You's warning was vindicated.

sentences.zh: 范成大帥蜀，游為參議官，以文字交，不拘禮法，人譏其頹放，因自號放翁。

translations.literal: Fan Chengda commanded Shu; You served as deliberation officer; they exchanged writings and did not constrain themselves by ritual — people mocked his dissolute freedom, and he styled himself Old Man Let-Go.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chengda commanded Sichuan; You served as deliberation officer. They exchanged writings without ritual constraint; critics mocked his dissolute freedom, and he styled himself Old Man Let-Go.

sentences.zh: 後累遷江西常平提舉。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly promoted to Jiangxi Ever-Normal Granary intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Jiangxi Ever-Normal Granary intendant.

sentences.zh: 江西水災。

translations.literal: Jiangxi suffered flooding.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi was struck by flooding.

sentences.zh: 奏：「撥義倉振濟，檄諸郡發粟以予民。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Allocate the charity granaries for relief and dispatch orders to all prefectures to release grain for the people."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Allocate charity granaries for relief and order all prefectures to release grain to the people."

sentences.zh: 召還，給事中趙汝愚駁之，遂與祠。

translations.literal: Recalled, Supervising Censor Zhao Ruyu rejected this and he was given a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, Supervising Censor Zhao Ruyu rejected the policy and he was given a sinecure.

sentences.zh: 起知嚴州，過闕，陛辭，上諭曰：「嚴陵山水勝處，職事之暇，可以賦詠自適。」

translations.literal: He was raised to prefect of Yanzhou; passing the palace he took leave at audience; the emperor instructed him: "Yanling is a place of fine mountains and waters; in leisure from duty you may compose poetry for your own pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Yanzhou. At leave-taking audience the emperor said: "Yanling has fine mountains and waters; in leisure from duty you may compose poetry for pleasure."

sentences.zh: 再召入見，上曰：「卿筆力回斡甚善，非他人可及。」

translations.literal: Summoned again for audience, the emperor said: "Your brushwork turns and weaves exceedingly well — others cannot match it."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned again, the emperor said: "Your brush turns and weaves exceedingly well — no one else matches it."

sentences.zh: 除軍器少監。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Armory.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Armory.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，遷禮部郎中兼實錄院檢討官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Rites concurrently Veritable Records reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 1 (1190) he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Rites, concurrently Veritable Records reviser.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰二年，以孝宗、光宗兩朝實錄及三朝史未就，詔游權同修國史、實錄院同修撰，免奉朝請，尋兼秘書監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiatai, because the veritable records of Xiaozong and Guangzong and the history of three reigns were not complete, an edict ordered You to serve concurrently as associate compiler of the National History and associate reviser of the Veritable Records, exempt from court attendance, and soon concurrently Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiatai 2 (1202), with Xiaozong's and Guangzong's veritable records and the three-reign history unfinished, an edict ordered You to serve as associate National History compiler and Veritable Records reviser, exempt from court attendance, soon concurrently Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年，書成，遂升寶章閣待制，致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year the books were complete; he was then promoted to Attendant of the Baozhang Pavilion and retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the books were complete; he was promoted to Baozhang Pavilion attendant and retired.

sentences.zh: 游才氣超逸，尤長於詩。

translations.literal: You's talent and spirit were transcendent; he was especially accomplished in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: You's talent and spirit were transcendent; he was especially masterful in poetry.

sentences.zh: 晚年再出，為韓侂胄撰《南園》、《閱古泉記》，見譏清議。

translations.literal: In his later years he emerged again and for Han Tuozhou wrote the records of the Southern Garden and the Yuegu Spring — he was mocked by pure critics.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he emerged again to write the Southern Garden and Yuegu Spring records for Han Tuozhou — earning mockery from moral critics.

sentences.zh: 朱熹嘗言：「其能太高，跡太近，恐為有力者所牽挽，不得全其晚節。」

translations.literal: Zhu Xi once said: "His ability is too high and his tracks too near — I fear he will be pulled by the powerful and unable to preserve his late integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi once said: "His talent is too high and his tracks too near power — I fear the powerful will pull him and he will not preserve his late integrity."

sentences.zh: 蓋有先見之明焉。

translations.literal: He truly had foresight.
translations.idiomatic: It was true foresight.

sentences.zh: 嘉定二年卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiading he died at age eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiading 2 (1210) at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 方信孺

translations.literal: Fang Xinru
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xinru (section)

sentences.zh: 方信孺，字孚若，興化軍人。

translations.literal: Fang Xinru, styled Furuo, was a native of the Xinghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xinru, courtesy name Furuo, came from the Xinghua garrison.

sentences.zh: 有雋材，未冠能文，周必大、楊萬里見而異之。

translations.literal: He had outstanding talent; before coming of age he could write; Zhou Bida and Yang Wanli saw him and were struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: He had outstanding talent; before coming of age he could write. Zhou Bida and Yang Wanli were struck by him.

sentences.zh: 以父崧卿蔭，補番禺縣尉。

translations.literal: Through his father Songqing's yin privilege he was appointed sheriff of Panyu County.
translations.idiomatic: By his father Songqing's yin privilege he was appointed sheriff of Panyu County.

sentences.zh: 盜劫海賈，信孺捕之，盜方沙聚分鹵獲，惶駭欲趨舟，信孺已使人負盜舟去矣，乃悉縛盜，不失一人。

translations.literal: Bandits robbed maritime merchants; Xinru captured them; the bandits were dividing the loot on the sand when, panic-stricken, they tried to rush to their boats — Xinru had already had their boats carried off; he bound all the bandits without losing a single man.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits robbed maritime merchants. Xinru captured them while they divided loot on the sand; panic-stricken, they rushed for their boats — but Xinru had already had the boats removed. He bound every bandit without losing one.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄舉恢復之謀，諸將僨軍，邊釁不已。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou raised the plan of recovery; the generals ruined the army and border incidents did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou launched the recovery campaign; generals ruined the army and border clashes continued.

sentences.zh: 朝廷尋悔，金人亦厭兵，乃遣韓元靚來使，而都督府亦再遣壯士遺敵書，然皆莫能得其要領。

translations.literal: The court soon repented; the Jurchens also wearied of war and sent Han Yuanjing as envoy, while the command headquarters also twice sent brave men to deliver letters to the enemy — yet none could grasp the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon repented; the Jurchens also wearied of war and sent Han Yuanjing as envoy. The command headquarters twice sent bold men with letters to the enemy — yet none grasped the essentials.

sentences.zh: 近臣薦信孺可使，自蕭山丞召赴都，命以使事。

translations.literal: A close minister recommended Xinru as suitable for the mission; from Xiangshan assistant magistrate he was summoned to the capital and ordered to the diplomatic task.
translations.idiomatic: A close minister recommended Xinru for the mission. From Xiangshan assistant magistrate he was summoned to the capital and charged with diplomacy.

sentences.zh: 信孺曰：「開釁自我，金人設問首謀，當何以答之？」

translations.literal: Xinru said: "We opened hostilities — if the Jurchens ask who was chief instigator, how shall we answer?"
translations.idiomatic: Xinru said: "We opened hostilities. If the Jurchens ask who the chief instigator was, how do we answer?"

sentences.zh: 侂胄矍然。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was startled.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was visibly startled.

sentences.zh: 假朝奉郎、樞密院檢詳文字，充樞密院參謀官，持督帥張岩書通問於金國元帥府。

translations.literal: Given temporary rank as Court Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement and Detailed Examiner of Documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs, he served as staff officer at the Bureau of Military Affairs, bearing Commander Zhang Yan's letter to communicate with the Jin Grand Marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Given temporary rank as Court Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement and Detailed Examiner at the Bureau of Military Affairs, he served as staff officer there, bearing Commander Zhang Yan's letter to the Jin Grand Marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 至濠州，金帥紇石烈子仁之止於獄中，露刃環守之，絕其薪水，要以五事。

translations.literal: Reaching Haozhou, the Jin commander He Shilie Ziren detained him in prison, surrounded him with bare blades, cut off fuel and water, and demanded five things.
translations.idiomatic: At Haozhou the Jin commander He Shilie Ziren detained him in prison, ringed him with bare blades, cut off fuel and water, and demanded five concessions.

sentences.zh: 信孺曰：「反俘、歸幣可也，縛送首謀，於古無之，稱藩、割地，則非臣子所忍言。」

translations.literal: Xinru said: "Returning captives and tribute coins can be done; sending bound the chief instigator has no precedent in antiquity; declaring vassalage and ceding territory — these a subject cannot bear to speak."
translations.idiomatic: Xinru said: "Returning captives and tribute coins — yes. Sending bound the chief instigator has no ancient precedent. Declaring vassalage and ceding territory — a subject cannot bear to speak of these."

sentences.zh: 子仁怒曰：「若不望生還耶？」

translations.literal: Ziren angrily said: "Do you not hope to return alive?"
translations.idiomatic: Ziren shouted angrily: "Do you expect to return alive?"

sentences.zh: 信孺曰：「吾將命出國門時，已置生死度外矣。」

translations.literal: Xinru said: "When I received my commission and left the nation's gate, I already placed life and death outside myself."
translations.idiomatic: Xinru said: "When I received my commission and left the nation's gate, I had already set life and death aside."

sentences.zh: 至汴，見金左丞相、都元帥完顏宗浩，出就傳舍。

translations.literal: Reaching Bian, he saw Jin's Left Chief Councillor and Grand Marshal Wanyan Zonghao and went out to the guest lodging.
translations.idiomatic: At Kaifeng he saw Jin Left Chief Councillor and Grand Marshal Wanyan Zonghao and withdrew to guest quarters.

sentences.zh: 宗浩使將命者來，堅持五說，且謂：「稱藩、割地，自有故事。」

translations.literal: Zonghao sent the bearer of commands; he firmly held to the five demands and also said: "Declaring vassalage and ceding territory — these have precedents."
translations.idiomatic: Zonghao sent his envoy, firmly holding to the five demands and saying: "Vassalage and cession have precedents."

sentences.zh: 信孺曰：「昔靖康倉卒割三鎮，紹興以太母故暫屈，今日顧可用為故事耶？

translations.literal: Xinru said: "In Jingkang the three prefectures were hastily ceded; in Shaoxing there was temporary submission for the empress dowager's sake — can these be used as precedents today?
translations.idiomatic: Xinru said: "At Jingkang the three prefectures were hastily ceded; at Shaoxing there was temporary submission for the empress dowager's sake — can these serve as precedents today?

sentences.zh: 此事不獨小臣不敢言，行府亦不敢奏也。

translations.literal: This matter not only your humble servant dares not speak of — the command headquarters also dares not memorialize it.
translations.idiomatic: Not only dare I not speak of this — the command headquarters dare not memorialize it either.

sentences.zh: 請面見丞相決之。」

translations.literal: I ask to see the chief councillor face to face and decide."
translations.idiomatic: I request an audience with the chief councillor to decide the matter."

sentences.zh: 將命者引而前，宗浩方坐幄中，陳兵見之，云：「五事不從，兵南下矣。」

translations.literal: The bearer of commands led him forward; Zonghao was seated in his tent with troops displayed to receive him, saying: "If the five matters are not accepted, troops will march south."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy led him forward. Zonghao sat in his tent with troops displayed and said: "Reject the five demands and troops march south."

sentences.zh: 信孺辯對不少詘。

translations.literal: Xinru argued in reply without the least yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Xinru argued back without yielding an inch.

sentences.zh: 宗浩叱之曰：「前日興兵，今日求和，何也？」

translations.literal: Zonghao shouted at him: "The other day you raised troops; today you seek peace — why?"
translations.idiomatic: Zonghao shouted: "Yesterday you raised troops; today you seek peace — why?"

sentences.zh: 信孺曰：「前日興兵復仇，為社稷也。

translations.literal: Xinru said: "The other day troops were raised for revenge — for the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Xinru said: "Yesterday troops were raised for revenge — for the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 今日屈己求和，為生靈也。」

translations.literal: Today we humbly seek peace — for the living people."
translations.idiomatic: Today we humble ourselves to seek peace — for the sake of the people."

sentences.zh: 宗浩不能詰，授以報書曰：「和與戰，俟再至決之。」

translations.literal: Zonghao could not refute him and gave him a reply letter saying: "Peace and war — wait until your next arrival to decide."
translations.idiomatic: Zonghao could not refute him and gave a reply: "Peace and war — wait until your next visit to decide."

sentences.zh: 信孺還，詔侍從、兩省、臺諫官議所以復命。

translations.literal: Xinru returned; an edict ordered attendant officials, the two secretariats, and censorial and remonstrance officials to deliberate on how to report back.
translations.idiomatic: Xinru returned. An edict ordered attendant officials, both secretariats, and censorial and remonstrance officials to debate the reply.

sentences.zh: 眾議還俘獲，罪首謀，增歲幣五萬，遣信孺再往。

translations.literal: Public opinion favored returning captives, punishing the chief instigator, increasing annual tribute by fifty thousand, and sending Xinru again.
translations.idiomatic: Consensus favored returning captives, punishing the chief instigator, increasing annual tribute by fifty thousand, and sending Xinru again.

sentences.zh: 時吳曦已誅，金人氣頗索，然猶執初議。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Xi had already been executed; Jin's spirit was somewhat slackened, yet they still held to the original demands.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi had already been executed; Jin's morale was somewhat slackened, yet they still held to the original demands.

sentences.zh: 信孺曰：「本朝謂增幣已為卑屈，況名分地界哉？

translations.literal: Xinru said: "Our court already considers increasing tribute humiliating — how much more name and territory?
translations.idiomatic: Xinru said: "Our court already considers increased tribute humiliating — how much more titles and territory?

sentences.zh: 且以曲直校之，本朝興兵在去年四月，若貽書誘吳曦，則去年三月也，其曲固有在矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, comparing right and wrong: our court raised troops last year in the fourth month; if enticing Wu Xi is counted, that was last year in the third month — the wrong already lies on their side.
translations.idiomatic: On right and wrong: we raised troops last April; enticing Wu Xi was last March — the wrong is already theirs.

sentences.zh: 如以強弱言之，若得滁、濠，我亦得泗、漣水。

translations.literal: If speaking of strength and weakness: if they took Chuzhou and Haozhou, we also took Si and Lianshui.
translations.idiomatic: On strength: if they took Chuzhou and Haozhou, we took Si and Lianshui.

sentences.zh: 若誇胥浦橋之勝，我亦有鳳凰山之捷。

translations.literal: If they boast of victory at Xupu Bridge, we also have victory at Fenghuang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: If they boast Xupu Bridge, we have Fenghuang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 若謂我不能下宿、壽，若圍廬、和、楚果能下乎？

translations.literal: If they say we cannot take Suzhou and Shouzhou — can they truly take Luzhou, Hezhou, and Chuzhou if besieged?
translations.idiomatic: If they say we cannot take Suzhou and Shouzhou — can they truly take Luzhou, Hezhou, and Chuzhou under siege?

sentences.zh: 五事已從其三，而猶不我聽，不過再交兵耳。」

translations.literal: Of the five matters, three are already accepted, yet they still will not heed us — nothing more than fighting again."
translations.idiomatic: Of five demands, three are already accepted, yet they still refuse — nothing remains but fighting again."

sentences.zh: 金人見信孺忠懇，乃曰：「割地之議姑寢，但稱藩不從，當以叔為伯，歲幣外，別犒師可也。」

translations.literal: Seeing Xinru's sincerity, the Jurchens then said: "The cession proposal may rest for now, but if declaring vassalage is not accepted, 'uncle' may become 'elder brother'; apart from annual tribute, a separate army reward may be given."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Xinru's sincerity, the Jurchens said: "Cession may rest for now, but if vassalage is refused, 'uncle' may become 'elder brother'; apart from tribute, a separate army reward may be paid."

sentences.zh: 信孺固執不許。

translations.literal: Xinru firmly held and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xinru firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 宗浩計窮，遂密與定約。

translations.literal: Zonghao's plans were exhausted; he then secretly fixed a treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghao's plans were exhausted; he secretly fixed a treaty.

sentences.zh: 復命，再差充通謝國信所參謀官，奉國書誓草及許通謝百萬緡抵汴。

translations.literal: Reporting back, he was again dispatched as staff officer of the Office of Credentials of Gratitude for the State and bore the state letter, oath draft, and promised gratitude payment of one million strings to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting back, he was again dispatched as staff officer of the Office of Credentials of Gratitude, bearing the state letter, oath draft, and promised gratitude payment of one million strings to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 宗浩變前說，怒信孺不曲折建白，遽以誓書來，有「誅戮禁錮」語。

translations.literal: Zonghao changed his earlier position, angry that Xinru had not tactfully memorialized, and hastily sent the oath letter containing language of "execution and imprisonment."
translations.idiomatic: Zonghao changed his earlier position, angry that Xinru had not tactfully reported upward, and hastily sent an oath letter containing language of "execution and imprisonment."

sentences.zh: 信孺不為動，將命曰：「此事非犒軍錢可了。」

translations.literal: Xinru was unmoved; the bearer of commands said: "This matter cannot be settled with army reward money alone."
translations.idiomatic: Xinru was unmoved. The envoy said: "This cannot be settled with army reward money alone."

sentences.zh: 別出事目。

translations.literal: Separate items were produced.
translations.idiomatic: Separate demands were produced.

sentences.zh: 信孺曰：「歲幣不可再增，故代以通謝錢。

translations.literal: Xinru said: "Annual tribute cannot be increased again — therefore gratitude money substitutes for it.
translations.idiomatic: Xinru said: "Tribute cannot be increased again — gratitude money substitutes for it.

sentences.zh: 今得此求彼，吾有隕首而已。」

translations.literal: Now getting this they seek that — I have only losing my head."
translations.idiomatic: Now they get this and seek that — I have only my head to lose."

sentences.zh: 將命曰：「不爾，丞相欲留公。」

translations.literal: The bearer of commands said: "Otherwise the chief councillor wishes to detain you."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said: "Otherwise the chief councillor wishes to detain you."

sentences.zh: 信孺曰：「留於此死，辱命亦死，不若死於此。」

translations.literal: Xinru said: "To die detained here, or to die disgracing my commission — better to die here."
translations.idiomatic: Xinru said: "Die detained here or die disgracing my commission — better to die here."

sentences.zh: 會蜀兵取散關，金人益疑。

translations.literal: When Shu troops took Sanshui Pass, the Jurchens grew more suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu forces seized Sanshui Pass, the Jurchens grew still more suspicious.

sentences.zh: 信孺還，言：「敵所欲者五事：割兩淮一，增歲幣二，犒軍三，索歸正等人四，其五不敢言。」

translations.literal: Xinru returned and said: "The enemy desires five things: ceding the two Huai — one; increasing annual tribute — two; army rewards — three; demanding returnees — four; the fifth he dares not speak."
translations.idiomatic: Xinru returned and said: "The enemy wants five things: cede the two Huai; increase tribute; army rewards; demand returnees; the fifth he dares not speak."

sentences.zh: 侂胄再三問，至厲聲詰之，信孺徐曰：「欲得太師頭耳。」

translations.literal: Tuozhou repeatedly asked, even harshly interrogating; Xinru slowly said: "They want the Grand Preceptor's head — that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou pressed repeatedly, even interrogating harshly. Xinru slowly said: "They want the Grand Preceptor's head — that is all."

sentences.zh: 侂胄大怒，奪三秩，臨江軍居住。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was greatly angered, stripped him of three ranks, and ordered him to reside in Linjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was furious, stripped him of three ranks, and ordered residence in Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 信孺自春至秋，使金三往返，以口舌折強敵，金人計屈情見，然憤其不屈，議用弗就。

translations.literal: From spring to autumn Xinru went to Jin three times back and forth; with words he bent the strong enemy; the Jurchens' plans were exhausted and their feelings exposed, yet angered by his unyielding, his appointment was not carried through.
translations.idiomatic: From spring to autumn Xinru traveled to Jin three times; with words alone he bent a strong enemy. Jin's plans were exhausted and their feelings exposed, yet angered by his refusal to yield, his appointment was not confirmed.

sentences.zh: 已而王柟出使，定和議，增幣、函首，皆前信孺所持不可者。

translations.literal: Soon Wang Nan went as envoy and fixed the peace agreement — increased tribute and the boxed head were both what Xinru had refused.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Nan went as envoy and fixed peace — increased tribute and the boxed head were both what Xinru had refused.

sentences.zh: 柟白廟堂：「信孺辯折敵酋於強愎未易告語之時，信孺當其難，柟當其易。

translations.literal: Nan reported to the court: "Xinru argued down the enemy chieftain when he was strong and stubborn and hard to reason with — Xinru bore the hard part, Nan the easy.
translations.idiomatic: Nan reported to court: "Xinru argued down the enemy chieftain when he was strong, stubborn, and hard to reason with — Xinru took the hard part, Nan the easy.

sentences.zh: 柟每見，金人必問信孺安在，公論所推，雖敵人不能掩也。」

translations.literal: Whenever Nan appeared, the Jurchens always asked where Xinru was — public opinion's esteem, even enemies cannot conceal."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I appeared, the Jurchens asked where Xinru was — public esteem that even enemies cannot hide."

sentences.zh: 乃詔信孺自便。

translations.literal: An edict then permitted Xinru to go where he wished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then allowed Xinru to go where he pleased.

sentences.zh: 尋知韶州，累遷淮東轉運判官兼提刑。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Shaozhou, repeatedly promoted to Eastern Huai transport vice intendant concurrently intendant for punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was prefect of Shaozhou, then repeatedly promoted to Eastern Huai transport vice intendant concurrently intendant for punishments.

sentences.zh: 知真州，即北山匱水築石堤，袤二十里，人莫知其所為。

translations.literal: As prefect of Zhenzhou, he immediately built a stone dike twenty li long at the foot of North Mountain to store water — no one knew his purpose.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Zhenzhou he built a twenty-li stone dike at North Mountain to impound water — no one knew why.

sentences.zh: 後金人薄儀真，守將決水匱以退敵，城乃獲全。

translations.literal: Later when the Jurchens pressed Yizhen, the defending general released the impounded water to repel the enemy and the city was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Jurchens pressed Yizhen, the defender released the impounded water to repel them and the city was saved.

sentences.zh: 山東初內附，信孺言：「豪傑不可以虛名駕馭，武夫不可以弱勢彈壓，宜選威望重臣，將精兵數萬，開幕山東，以主制客，以重馭輕，則可以包山東，固江北，而兩河在吾目中矣。」

translations.literal: When Shandong first submitted inward, Xinru said: "Heroes cannot be driven by empty reputation; military men cannot be suppressed by weak force — one should choose a heavy minister of prestige, lead several tens of thousands of elite troops, and establish headquarters in Shandong; using the host to control the guest and the heavy to govern the light, one can then envelop Shandong, secure the north of the river, and have the two He regions within our sight."
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong first submitted, Xinru said: "Heroes cannot be ruled by empty titles; soldiers cannot be controlled by weak force. Choose a prestigious minister, lead tens of thousands of elite troops, and establish headquarters in Shandong. With the host controlling the guest and weight governing lightness, Shandong can be enveloped, the north of the river secured, and the two He regions brought within sight."

sentences.zh: 坐責降三秩，再奉祠，稍復官。

translations.literal: He was punished by demotion of three ranks, again given a sinecure, and gradually had his office restored.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted three ranks, given a sinecure again, and gradually had his office restored.

sentences.zh: 信孺性豪爽，揮金如糞土，所至賓客滿其後車。

translations.literal: Xinru's nature was bold and generous; he spent gold like dirt; wherever he went guests filled the carriage behind him.
translations.idiomatic: Xinru was bold and generous, spending gold like dirt; wherever he went guests filled the carriages behind him.

sentences.zh: 使北時，年財三十。

translations.literal: When he went north on mission he was barely thirty.
translations.idiomatic: When he went north as envoy he was not yet thirty.

sentences.zh: 既齟齬歸，營居室岩竇，自放於詩酒。

translations.literal: After friction and return he built a dwelling among rocky caves and gave himself to poetry and wine.
translations.idiomatic: After his falling-out he built a dwelling among rocky caves and gave himself to poetry and wine.

sentences.zh: 後貲用竭，賓客益落，信孺尋亦死矣。

translations.literal: Later his wealth was exhausted and guests dwindled further; Xinru soon died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Later his wealth ran out and guests dwindled; Xinru soon died as well.

sentences.zh: 王柟，字汝良，大名人。

translations.literal: Wang Nan, styled Ruliang, was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Nan, courtesy name Ruliang, came from Daming.

sentences.zh: 祖倫，同簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lun concurrently served as Assistant Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lun had concurrently served as Assistant Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 倫使北死，孝宗訪求其孫之未祿者三人官之，柟其一也。

translations.literal: Lun died on a northern mission; Xiaozong sought his unappointed grandsons and gave three of them office — Nan was one.
translations.idiomatic: Lun died on a northern mission. Xiaozong sought unappointed grandsons and gave three office — Nan was one.

sentences.zh: 調通州海門尉。

translations.literal: He was assigned as sheriff of Haimen in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned sheriff of Haimen in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 乘輕舟入海濤，捕劇賊小吳郎，並其徒十七人獲之，獄成，不受賞。

translations.literal: Taking a light boat into the sea swells, he captured the notorious bandit Xiao Wulang and seventeen of his followers; when the case was complete he did not accept reward.
translations.idiomatic: Taking a light boat into ocean swells, he captured the notorious bandit Xiao Wulang and seventeen followers. When the case closed he refused reward.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄以恢復起兵端，天子思繼好息民，凡七遣使無成。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou raised troops for recovery; the Son of Heaven wished to renew good relations and rest the people — seven envoys were sent without success.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou launched the recovery campaign. The emperor wished to renew good relations and rest the people — seven envoys were sent without success.

sentences.zh: 續遣方信孺往，將有成說矣，坐白事忤侂胄得罪。

translations.literal: Fang Xinru was then sent and was about to reach agreement when, for reporting facts that offended Tuozhou, he was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xinru was then sent and nearly reached agreement, but offended Tuozhou by reporting facts and was punished.

sentences.zh: 欲再遣使，顧在廷無可者，近臣以柟薦，擢監登聞鼓院，假右司郎中，使持書北行。

translations.literal: Wishing to send an envoy again, yet seeing no one suitable at court, a close minister recommended Nan; he was promoted to director of the Palace Drum Petition Office, given temporary rank as Right Director in a ministry, and sent bearing a letter north.
translations.idiomatic: Wanting to send another envoy but finding no one suitable, a close minister recommended Nan. He was promoted director of the Palace Drum Petition Office, given temporary rank as Right Director, and sent north bearing a letter.

sentences.zh: 柟歸白其母，母曰：「而祖以忠死國，故恩及子孫。

translations.literal: Nan returned and told his mother; his mother said: "Your grandfather died loyally for the state — therefore favor reaches his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Nan returned to tell his mother. She said: "Your grandfather died loyally for the state — therefore favor reaches his descendants.

sentences.zh: 汝其勉旃，毋以吾老為念。」

translations.literal: You must exert yourself — do not think of my old age."
translations.idiomatic: Exert yourself — do not think of my old age."

sentences.zh: 乃拜命，疾驅抵敵所。

translations.literal: He then accepted the commission and galloped swiftly to the enemy's place.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted the commission and galloped to the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 金將烏骨論等四人列坐，問：「韓侂胄貴顯幾年矣？」

translations.literal: The Jin generals Wugulun and three others sat in a row and asked: "How many years has Han Tuozhou been noble and prominent?"
translations.idiomatic: Jin generals including Wugulun sat in a row and asked: "How long has Han Tuozhou been noble and prominent?"

sentences.zh: 柟對：「已十餘年，平章國事財二年耳。」

translations.literal: Nan answered: "Already more than ten years; as chief councillor of state affairs only two years."
translations.idiomatic: Nan answered: "More than ten years; as chief councillor only two."

sentences.zh: 又問：「今欲去此人可乎？」

translations.literal: They again asked: "If one wished to remove this man now, could it be done?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked again: "If we wished to remove this man now, could it be done?"

sentences.zh: 柟曰：「主上英斷，去之何難。」

translations.literal: Nan said: "Our ruler is brilliant and decisive — removing him would be nothing difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Nan said: "Our ruler is brilliant and decisive — removing him would be easy."

sentences.zh: 四人相顧而笑。

translations.literal: The four looked at one another and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: The four exchanged glances and laughed.

sentences.zh: 有完顏天寵者，袖出文書，云：「王柟雖持韓侂胄書，乃朝廷有旨遣其來元帥府議和，宜詳議以報。」

translations.literal: One Wanyan Tianchong drew out a document from his sleeve, saying: "Although Wang Nan bears Han Tuozhou's letter, the court has ordered him sent to the Grand Marshal's headquarters to discuss peace — it should be deliberated in detail for reply."
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Tianchong drew a document from his sleeve: "Though Wang Nan bears Han Tuozhou's letter, the court ordered him to the Grand Marshal's headquarters to discuss peace — deliberate in detail and reply."

sentences.zh: 於是金人知侂胄已誅，和議遂決。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Jurchens knew Tuozhou had already been executed and the peace agreement was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens then knew Tuozhou had been executed and peace was settled.

sentences.zh: 柟持金人牒歸，求函侂胄首，以起居郎許奕為通謝使，柟為通謝所參謀官。

translations.literal: Nan returned bearing the Jurchen document; they demanded Han Tuozhou's head in a box; Attendant Gentleman Xu Yi was made envoy of gratitude and Nan staff officer of the Office of Gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Nan returned with the Jurchen document demanding Tuozhou's head in a box. Attendant Gentleman Xu Yi was made envoy of gratitude; Nan served as staff officer of the Gratitude Office.

sentences.zh: 柟自軍前再還，議以侂胄首易淮、陝侵地，從之。

translations.literal: Nan returned again from the front and it was debated to exchange Tuozhou's head for Huai and Shan invaded territory — this was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Nan returned again from the front. The court debated exchanging Tuozhou's head for invaded Huai and Shan territory — and agreed.

sentences.zh: 柟奏：「和約之成，皆方信孺備嘗險阻再三將命之功，臣因人成事，乞錄信孺功而蠲其過。」

translations.literal: Nan memorialized: "The peace agreement was achieved entirely through Fang Xinru's repeated missions through danger and hardship — your servant accomplished it through another's work; I ask that Xinru's merit be recorded and his faults remitted."
translations.idiomatic: Nan memorialized: "Peace was achieved through Fang Xinru's repeated dangerous missions — I accomplished it through another's work. I ask that Xinru's merit be recorded and his faults remitted."

sentences.zh: 朝論以柟不掩人揚己多之。

translations.literal: Court opinion praised Nan for not concealing others' merit and boasting of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion praised Nan for not hiding others' merit to boast of himself.

sentences.zh: 守軍器少監，知楚州，累官至太府卿。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Director of the Armory, prefect of Chuzhou, and rose through offices to Director of the Court of the Imperial Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Director of the Armory, prefect of Chuzhou, and rose to Director of the Court of the Imperial Granary.

sentences.zh: 告歸，以右文殿修撰知太平州，加集英殿修撰，致仕。

translations.literal: Requesting retirement, as Right Culture Hall Compiler he was made prefect of Taiping Prefecture; promoted to Hall Compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence, he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Requesting retirement, as Right Culture Hall compiler he was prefect of Taiping; promoted to Hall Compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence, he retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈寶章閣待制。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted Attendant of the Baozhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At death he was posthumously granted Baozhang Pavilion attendant.

sentences.zh: 論曰：樓鑰渾厚正大，李大性直言不愧其先，任希夷請諡先儒，徐應龍在經筵多所裨益，莊夏、王阮、王質皆負其有為之才，卒奉祠去國。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Lou Yao was solid and upright; Li Daxing spoke straight without shaming his ancestors; Ren Xiyi requested posthumous titles for the early Confucians; Xu Yinglong in the lecture hall was of much benefit; Zhuang Xia, Wang Ruan, and Wang Zhi all possessed talent for action — yet in the end they received sinecures and left the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The judgment: Lou Yao was solid and upright; Li Daxing spoke plainly without shaming his line; Ren Xiyi sought posthumous titles for the early Confucians; Xu Yinglong benefited the lecture hall greatly; Zhuang Xia, Wang Ruan, and Wang Zhi all had talent for action — yet all ended with sinecures, leaving the capital.

sentences.zh: 陸遊學廣而望隆，晚為韓侂胄著堂記，君子惜之，抑《春秋》責賢者備也。

translations.literal: Lu You's learning was broad and his repute lofty; in old age he wrote hall records for Han Tuozhou — gentlemen regretted it; yet is this not also the Spring and Autumn Annals' full standard for the worthy?
translations.idiomatic: Lu You's learning was broad and his repute lofty; in old age he wrote hall records for Han Tuozhou — gentlemen regretted it; yet does not the Spring and Autumn Annals hold the worthy to the fullest standard?

sentences.zh: 方信孺年少奉使，而以意氣折金人。

translations.literal: Fang Xinru at a young age served as envoy and with spirit bent the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xinru at a young age served as envoy and with sheer spirit bent the Jurchens.

sentences.zh: 王柟北歸，請錄信孺之功，長者哉！

translations.literal: Wang Nan, returning from the north, asked that Xinru's merit be recorded — how worthy of an elder!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Nan, returning from the north, asked that Xinru's merit be recorded — what elder's grace!
